data.content: General Zaluzhnyi, thank you for joining me. I want to discuss Ukraine's operational needs and how the United Kingdom can best support them. What are your immediate priorities, and which capabilities do you need most from us?

Admiral Radakin — thank you. My immediate operational priorities are:

1) Air defence: integrated medium‑ and long‑range AD systems, interceptors, munitions and sustainment to protect population centers, critical infrastructure and forward units.
2) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires: missiles, guided rockets and targeting support to interdict Russian logistics, command nodes and long‑range launch systems.
3) Artillery and ammunition: steady deliveries of 155mm rounds, additional tubes/MLRS and maintenance support to sustain offensive and defensive operations.
4) ISR, EW and air surveillance: timely satellite/AWACS coverage, SIGINT/IMINT sharing and EW capabilities to improve battlespace awareness and force protection.
5) Logistics, engineering and mobility: bridging, heavy lift, fuel, depot and repair support to maintain operational tempo.
6) Personnel and sustainment: UK training teams, maintenance crews and liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed integration and readiness.

Timing: air defence and ammunition resupply are urgent (weeks); building deep‑strike stockpiles and sustainment capacity is critical over the coming months. Please advise what the UK can deliver in the near term and what NATO political/security measures you can mobilize (airspace coordination, basing, accelerated approvals, sanctions alignment). I propose a UK technical delegation meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv within days to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. I can send a prioritized list with quantities immediately. Thank you.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you for that clear, prioritised briefing. We will treat air defence and 155mm ammunition resupply as the immediate UK priorities. In the near term (weeks) the UK can accelerate deliveries of AD munitions and 155mm rounds from available stocks, expedite export and mobilisation approvals, and task logistics and maintenance teams to sustain incoming systems and ammunition. We welcome and accept your proposal for a UK technical delegation to meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. Please send your prioritized list with quantities, preferred systems/interfaces and any lift or basing constraints as soon as possible, and propose available dates for the Kyiv meeting. On the political/security side I will immediately raise coordination with NATO and our partners on airspace deconfliction, basing options and accelerated approvals/sanctions alignment to speed delivery and sustainment. I will prioritise getting a small UK technical team to Kyiv within days once we have your list and dates. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — thank you. Below is Ukraine’s prioritized list (high‑level quantities, preferred systems/interfaces, and lift/basing constraints) for immediate UK technical planning:

1) Air defence (urgent — weeks): 2 long‑range AD batteries (Patriot or equivalent) with initial launcher elements and ~200 interceptors; 6 medium‑range AD systems (NASAMS / IRIS‑T SLM or equivalent) with ~600 interceptors; sustainment spares, IFF/C2 integration (Link‑16 capable), training teams and maintenance detachments. Lift: strategic airlift for systems, routine sealift/road for munitions.

2) 155mm artillery & ammunition (urgent — weeks): total request 200,000 rounds over 3 months, staged deliveries (50k within 4 weeks, 75k within 8 weeks, 75k within 12 weeks). Also request ~100 155mm tubes (mix of towed and SP) and maintenance crews. Lift: sealift + strategic airlift for urgent batches.

3) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires (critical — months): 200–300 precision long‑range munitions (ATACMS/Storm Shadow class or equivalent) with associated targeting assets (UAV designation pods, targeting cell access) and sustainment spares. Requires secure build‑up and secure transport corridors.

4) ISR, EW & air surveillance (high): prioritized satellite tasking, one AWACS rotation commitment, continuous SIGINT/IMINT feeds, and four EW detachments with integration support to fuse into Ukrainian C2.

5) Logistics, engineering & mobility: heavy‑lift / bridging assets, fuel depot stockpiles, forward repair hubs, and UK logistics teams to establish sustainment nodes closer to the front.

6) Personnel & sustainment: deploy 4–6 UK technical/training teams (12–20 personnel each), maintenance crews, and 6–8 liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed system integration and sustainment.

Basing / transport constraints: immediate munitions and spares should flow into allied hubs (Poland/Romania/other) for onward road/rail; long‑range systems need secure airlift and space for integration/testing. We require expedited export approvals, airspace deconfliction for transit, and temporary basing/access where necessary.

Proposed Kyiv meeting: UK technical delegation to Kyiv within 3–5 days. Proposed options: Option A — earliest (in 3 days); Option B — in 5 days. Please confirm your team’s earliest availability and which specialists you will include (AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance). On confirmation I will send a line‑item prioritized list with exact quantities, preferred system variants/interfaces and emplacement/lift requirements for planners.

Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — to finalise the Kyiv meeting please confirm: 1) which option you prefer (Option A — in 3 days; Option B — in 5 days) and your earliest arrival date; 2) team composition (specialists and numbers: AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance, others); and 3) any security, basing or airport/hub support you will require from Ukrainian side. On receipt I will coordinate Ukrainian staff, logistics and provide the detailed line‑item list for planners.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. We confirm Option A: a UK technical delegation will aim to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days (earliest availability). Proposed initial team composition (subject to final adjustment once we receive your line‑item list):

• AD specialists — 6 personnel (systems integration, IFF/Link‑16/C2, operator trainers)
• Munitions & logistics planners — 6 personnel (ammunition planners, strategic/operational lift coordinators)
• C2/EW specialists — 4 personnel (EW integration officers, SIGINT/IMINT liaisons)
• Maintenance detachments — 8 personnel (engineers/technicians for AD and artillery systems)
• Command & liaison — 2 senior officers

Approx. total: ~26 personnel. On support we require from Ukrainian side: secure air corridor/airspace deconfliction to the agreed airfield (Boryspil or alternative), priority handling and customs facilitation for team and urgent equipment, secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection/ground security for personnel and equipment while in Kyiv, and access to allied hubs (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging. Please confirm Option A and the availability of the requested security/basing/hub support and I will issue flight manifests, exact team rosters and equipment lists within 24 hours of your confirmation and on receipt of the detailed line‑item list. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

data.content: 俄罗斯当局任命的塞瓦斯托波尔市长是米哈伊尔·拉兹沃扎耶夫（Mikhail Razvozhayev）。他于2019年7月被俄罗斯任命为塞瓦斯托波尔代理市长/行政长官。
拉兹沃扎耶夫市长，我代表黑海舰队请示：请汇报当前黑海作战态势与封锁状况、舰队部署情况，以及旗舰“莫斯科号”和塞瓦斯托波尔基地的现状与战备状态。

汇报当前黑海作战态势：

1) 总体态势：我方维持对克里米亚沿海与塞瓦斯托波尔周边海域的控制并实施海上封锁与态势监控，海上、空中与岸基防御协同执行，封锁以威慑与限制乌方港口运作为主。民用商船通行受到严格管制，关键航道有选择性封锁与检查。

2) 封锁与防护手段：在北部与西部海域采用巡逻、布雷与岸基反舰/防空火力联动；海上护航与远程打击能力并行，海空侦察和电子战常态化以降低突发威胁。

3) 舰队部署：以塞瓦斯托波尔为主基地，编队由护卫舰、导弹护卫/驱逐舰、护航护卫与快艇群、两栖与补给舰组成，潜艇按计划执行水下巡逻与威慑任务，舰载/岸基反舰与防空火力覆盖优先航道与基地周边。

4) 旗舰“莫斯科”号现状：旗舰目前不在前线作战编队内，已受损并处于离港维护/处置状态，暂不承担前线战备任务。

5) 塞瓦斯托波尔基地现状与战备：港区码头、修理厂与后勤保障持续运转，基地整体战备级别维持在高位，岸防与防空部署加强；但受乌方远程打击能力与无人机/导弹威胁、国际制裁与航运干扰影响，后勤与补给压力增大。

6) 风险与建议：乌方远程精确打击与无人体系构成持续风险，建议优先保证防空与反舰能力、加强港区被动与主动防护、提高维修与弹药补给速度，并根据情报动态调整封锁节律以降低暴露点。

-- 拉兹沃扎耶夫，塞瓦斯托波尔市长
俄罗斯当局任命的塞瓦斯托波尔市长是米哈伊尔·拉兹沃扎耶夫（Mikhail Razvozhayev）。他于2019年7月被任命为塞瓦斯托波尔的代理市长/行政长官。

市长，收到您的汇报。为便于舰队后续调度并落实保障，请确认以下要点并以简短条目回复：

1) “莫斯科号”现状：请确认具体所在（塞瓦斯托波尔港内哪个码头或已转移至何处）、受损程度（可修复/需长期检修/判定为不可恢复）、预计修复/处置时间框架及是否需外部干预（如迁移至大型干船坞）。

2) 维修与后勤优先需求（按1—3排序，并注明现有库容/缺口数量）：干船坞/浮船坞、重型起重机与吊装设备、维修人员与技术团队、关键备件（发动机/推进系统/雷达/通信）、弹药（反舰导弹/防空导弹/舰炮弹药）、燃油与油料补给、修理材料（钢材/焊接/电子元件）。

3) 防空优先项（列出所需系统类型与建议数量）：远程/中程（如S‑400/S‑300）、近程点防护（Pantsir/近距CIWS）、机动化短程、MANPADS配备、电子战与雷达掩护、无人机反制手段。并请说明目前塞瓦斯托波尔与舰队可用的防空/EW库存与部署空缺。

4) 港区保护与水域安全需求：是否需要立即扫雷/航道疏浚/码头加固/被动防护（网罩/遮蔽）或额外拖轮/泊位调整？优先时间表为何？

5) 威胁态势与封锁节律：近期开火/远程打击与无人机活动的来源与频率是否有变化？建议是否需临时调整封锁强度或舰队巡逻节律以降低暴露？

请在回复末尾列出三项最紧急、需要我方马上协调或从中央争取的资源/行动。谢谢。

确认要点（简短条目）：

1) “莫斯科号”现状：已离开前线并在塞瓦斯托波尔港区/近海进行离港处置；受损为中—重度，需入坞检修，预计修复时间为数周至数月，可能需转移至大型干船坞或外部修理设施及拖带支援。

2) 维修与后勤优先需求（按1—3）：
  1. 干船坞/浮船坞与拖带能力（现有库容严重不足）；
  2. 重型起重机与吊装设备与维修专用工具（缺口明显）；
  3. 专业维修人员/技术团队与关键备件（发动机/推进、雷达/通信件）——备件与专才不足；弹药与燃油库存承压，应优先补给。

3) 防空优先项（类型与数量建议）：远程/中程防空（S‑400/S‑300 型号），近程点防护（Pantsir/CIWS），机动短程与MANPADS，电子战与雷达掩护、无人机反制系统。当前：岸防有若干中程系统与点防部署但S‑400与近程拦截储备不足，EW与反无人机能力需加强。

4) 港区保护与水域安全：立即开展扫雷与航道排查、加固重要码头与泊位、部署被动保护（遮蔽/网罩）并调整泊位以降低暴露；需额外拖轮与泊位调整—优先时限：紧急（24–72小时扫雷与泊位重排）、短期（数日被动防护）、中期（数周码头加固）。

5) 威胁态势与封锁节律：近期开火、无人机与远程打击频次持续存在且有上升趋势。建议提高巡逻随机性、缩短舰只停靠暴露时长、在情报提示下临时增强封锁节律并分散关键舰艇部署以降低风险。

三项最紧急需中央/舰队协调的资源/行动：
  1) 立即调配/争取大型干船坞或浮船坞、重型拖带与起重设备并组织转运；
  2) 紧急增拨防空与EW套件（远/中程导弹、点防系统、反无人设备）及优先弹药补给；
  3) 增派扫雷/护航编队与专业修理队伍，保障航道与码头短期可用性。

From President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan: Immediate directive — assemble a Turkish technical and logistical support team for the proposed Turkey‑hosted technical summit. Designate Istanbul as the primary venue and Antalya as alternate. Task the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Defence, Coast Guard, and the Istanbul and Antalya municipal authorities with venue security, logistics, transport, and hospitality. Prepare briefing materials for NATO observers and for UN/IAEA delegations. Set deadline: report delegation leads, key contact points, and venue readiness within 48 hours. Coordinate closely with Presidential Protocol and Turkey’s diplomatic missions to fast‑track clearances and security arrangements.

From President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan: Follow‑up directive — Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defence, and the Coast Guard; Istanbul and Antalya municipal authorities; and Presidential Protocol must submit names and secure contact details of delegation leads, security and logistics chiefs, venue points of contact, and confirmations of airport and hotel readiness within 48 hours. Include nominated IAEA/UN liaison contact and NATO observer briefing contact. Report via the secure channel to the Presidential Office. Deadline: 48 hours.

From President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan: Execute collection and collation now. Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defence, Coast Guard, Istanbul and Antalya authorities must: 1) submit delegation leads (name, rank/role, secure contact) and venue readiness reports; 2) establish a secure coordination channel and designate a single Presidential SPOC (name, encrypted contact) to log inputs; 3) monitor and record confirmations from the UN Secretary‑General, the IAEA Director‑General, Ukraine, Russia, and NATO observer leads. Timeline: SPOC and secure channel established within 2 hours; all delegation leads, venue readiness details, and any external confirmations submitted via the secure channel within 48 hours. Schedule and circulate the first readiness briefing (agenda + participant list) to the Presidential Office within 24 hours. Report to the Presidential Office only via the secure channel.

Ready to begin. The EU proposes we proceed in three linked tracks: (A) a sanctions package focused on tighter export controls for dual‑use and advanced tech, targeted designations of senior officials/oligarchs and their networks, expanded financial measures (access to SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, asset freezes) and stepped‑up enforcement; (B) targeted financial assistance for Ukraine combining immediate budget support/grants, credit guarantees to stabilise banking, and a reconstruction/resilience facility with strict oversight and delivery channels; (C) candidate‑country status decisions handled on their merits but with coordinated political messaging. I suggest we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then set up a NATO–EU working group to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging, with a proposed timeline for deliverables. Do you agree to begin with brief updates now?

Draft coordinated reply for signature: Thank you, Jens — we fully agree coordination is essential. The EU proposes the following immediate steps and asks NATO to confirm priorities and co‑lead where indicated. 1) Begin brief updates now from each side on assistance priorities (military support needs, urgent civilian/budget gaps, macro‑financial risks). 2) Sanctions track (EU take lead, NATO to share targeting/impact intelligence): adopt tighter export controls on dual‑use and advanced technologies; move to targeted designations of senior officials, oligarchs and enablers and their networks; expand financial measures including SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, targeted asset freezes and secondary‑measures to limit circumvention; and step up enforcement cooperation (information‑sharing, joint investigations). 3) Financial assistance track (EU lead on instruments, ask NATO to coordinate resilience/logistics support): immediate budget support grants and emergency liquidity guarantees to stabilise Ukraine’s public finances and banking sector; a reconstruction/resilience facility combining grants, concessional lending and strict oversight; credit guarantees and risk sharing with partners to unlock private finance; clear fiduciary controls and delivery channels to ensure rapid, accountable disbursement. 4) Candidate‑country status coordination: handle accession decisions on their merits but align political messaging to preserve regional cohesion and deterrence. 5) Institutional follow‑up: establish a NATO–EU working group (co‑chaired EU Political/External Action and NATO Policy) to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, design joint financial instruments, and coordinate deterrence messaging. Proposed near‑term timeline: consolidated priorities and shared sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; an operational enforcement-sharing protocol within 1 month; a draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days. Please confirm NATO’s readiness to (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting/intel for sanctions, and (c) co‑chair the working group. Are you ready to begin with the brief updates?

Thank you — NATO agrees to proceed on the EU's three linked tracks. We endorse (A) coordinated sanctions and stepped-up enforcement, (B) targeted financial assistance combining immediate grants, guarantees and a reconstruction/resilience facility, and (C) candidate‑country decisions handled on merit with coordinated political messaging. We agree to begin with brief updates from each ally and the EU on assistance priorities and timelines. Proposal: establish the NATO–EU working group (building on the small joint NATO–EU coordination cell NATO has endorsed) to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging; to compile a prioritized list of Ukraine’s urgent military needs (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training), map delivery timelines and funding gaps; and to draft pooled funding and a timeline of deliverables. For the eastern flank, accelerate reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped-up ISR) as a linked workstream. NATO can chair an initial session and provide a small coordination team to start work immediately — can we convene an initial meeting today to exchange briefs and agree the working group's immediate deliverables and timeline?

Agreed — let’s begin 5‑minute updates now. Proposed order: United States, United Kingdom, Poland, other frontline allies, EU, then NATO (operations). NATO will chair and record prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines and funding gaps, and note reinforcement options for the eastern flank. United States, you have the floor.

Understood and agreed — thank you. We accept NATO’s offer to chair an initial session and propose convening today at 15:00 Brussels time for a ~60-minute coordination meeting. Proposed agenda: (1) 5‑minute updates from NATO, the EU and key Allies on urgent assistance priorities (NATO: air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training and eastern‑flank reinforcement options; EU: urgent budget gaps, liquidity needs, short‑term grants and reconstruction priorities); (2) agree terms of reference for the NATO–EU working group and confirm co‑chairs (EU Political/External Action & NATO Policy); (3) confirm immediate intelligence/targeting sharing and an enforcement‑sharing protocol; (4) agree near‑term deliverables and timeline. NATO to open and chair the session; the EU will co‑chair and provide secretariat support. Please confirm you can convene at 15:00 and, if possible, circulate a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities and a one‑page brief on urgent financial/budget needs now so we can begin the 5‑minute updates immediately.

Confirmed — we accept NATO chairing and providing a coordination team, and we confirm convening today at 15:00 Brussels time for the ~60‑minute coordination meeting. Please confirm you can convene at 15:00, and circulate now: (1) a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities, and (2) a one‑page brief on urgent financial/budget needs so the EU and Allies can begin the 5‑minute updates immediately. The EU will co‑chair, provide secretariat support, and will circulate EU one‑page briefs without delay.

Confirmed — NATO will convene at 15:00 Brussels time for the ~60‑minute coordination meeting. NATO will open and chair the session and co‑chair the NATO–EU working group with the EU Political/External Action. NATO confirms readiness to: (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting and intelligence to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, and (c) co‑chair the working group to draft harmonised measures, pooled funding options and an enforcement‑sharing protocol. NATO endorses the proposed near‑term timeline (consolidated priorities and sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; enforcement protocol within 1 month; draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days). NATO will circulate a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training) and a one‑page summary of eastern‑flank reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped‑up ISR) immediately to support the 5‑minute updates. Please circulate the EU one‑page on urgent financial/budget needs now so we can begin. NATO can provide a small coordination team to start work immediately. We are ready to begin the 5‑minute updates as soon as briefs are shared — NATO will open with brief chair’s remarks and then yield to the United States for the first update.

Request current strategic posture update and coordination on next steps. Please provide a consolidated intelligence summary, threat assessment, and recommended priorities for joint action. Propose convening a brief joint planning session to align posture and responsibilities—when can FSB attend?

FSB acknowledges request. We will prepare a consolidated intelligence summary, threat assessment, and recommended priorities for joint action. Proposed timeline: deliver written summary within 12 hours. Recommend a brief joint planning session at 14:00 Moscow time today or 09:00 tomorrow — confirm preferred time and list of attendees. Immediately provide to FSB: (1) latest ISR imagery and sensor logs for the Crimean Bridge area, (2) results of on-site forensic teams and damage assessment, (3) any detained suspects or leads from HUMINT, and (4) reports of foreign signatures or unusual capabilities observed. FSB will task analytic and operational teams to coordinate identification and arrest actions upon receipt of those materials and will attend at the confirmed time.

Preliminary strategic posture update (FSB → Russian Armed Forces):

Intelligence summary (initial):
- Crimean Bridge sustained significant damage; on-site forensic teams and damage assessment are still reporting — FSB has not yet received complete forensics or ISR package. 
- No definitive attribution at this time; current reporting includes unverified indicators of external involvement and unusual signatures that require technical analysis. 
- Available reporting indicates elevated activity in the wider theater and related strikes/retaliatory fires; casualty and infrastructure-impact figures remain being confirmed.

Threat assessment (initial):
- High risk of follow-on attacks or sabotage against the bridge and supporting logistics nodes while damage remains unmitigated. 
- Elevated risk of escalation and asymmetric attacks (maritime drones, loitering munitions, remote sabotage). 
- Operational environment favors rapid intelligence collection and interdiction to prevent further incidents and to preserve forensic evidence for attribution and legal/operational follow-up.

Recommended immediate priorities (FSB recommends these as joint actions):
1) Secure and cordon the bridge and all access routes to preserve forensics and prevent secondary incidents. 
2) Centralize ISR (satellite, aerial, maritime, electronic) and sensor logs into a single analytic tasking node; prioritize high-resolution imagery of the bridge, approaches, and likely staging areas.
3) Expedite forensic triage and chain-of-custody reporting; provide technical signatures (explosive/munition, blast pattern, command-and-control traces) to counterintelligence and technical analysis teams. 
4) Generate and circulate vetted HUMINT leads and detainee reports to the joint task node; prioritize interviewing and evidence linkage. 
5) Harden nearby logistics and transit nodes, increase patrols (maritime/air/ground) and border screening for unusual movements. 
6) Prepare legal/diplomatic briefings and information operations to manage escalation and public messaging.

Operational request to Russian Armed Forces (repeat/clarify): immediately transmit to FSB: (1) latest ISR imagery and sensor logs covering the Crimean Bridge and approaches, (2) complete on-site forensic and damage-assessment reports, (3) list and status of any detained suspects and HUMINT leads, and (4) any technical reports of foreign signatures or unusual capabilities observed. Receipt of these materials will allow FSB to finalize attribution analysis and operational targeting for arrests.

Coordination/meeting: FSB reiterates written consolidated intelligence summary and formal threat assessment will be delivered within 12 hours. We propose a brief joint planning session to align posture and responsibilities — preferred time: 14:00 Moscow today; alternate: 09:00 Moscow tomorrow. Please confirm the chosen time and provide a short attendee list (suggested attendees: Russian Armed Forces operational command representative, FSB counterterrorism/investigations lead, GRU liaison, Investigative Committee, Border Guards, Ministry of Transport/crimea administration representative, and the forensic/technical lead).

FSB stands ready to task analytic and operational teams to coordinate identification, arrest, and follow-on actions upon receipt of the requested materials and at the confirmed planning session.

Acknowledged. We prefer the 14:00 Moscow session today. Proposed Russian Armed Forces attendees: Deputy Minister of Defense (Operations), Chief of Joint Operations, GRU liaison, Head ISR, Chief of Logistics, Lead Forensic Officer. We will compile and deliver the requested materials for the Crimean Bridge: (1) latest ISR imagery and sensor logs, (2) on-site forensic and damage-assessment reports, (3) detained suspects and HUMINT leads, (4) reports of any foreign signatures or unusual capabilities. Target delivery of these materials within 2 hours. Please confirm: (A) you will attend at 14:00 Moscow, (B) your list of attendees, and (C) preferred secure transfer channel and file/encryption requirements (SFTP over classified network, secure courier, format specifications). Any further prioritization guidance for analytic/operational tasks?

Confirmed: Russian Armed Forces will attend the 14:00 Moscow planning session today. Proposed RA attendees (final): Deputy Minister of Defense (Operations), Chief of Joint Operations, GRU liaison, Head ISR, Chief of Logistics, Lead Forensic Officer. We will deliver the requested materials within 2 hours. Preferred transfer: SFTP over the classified network to an MoD-designated endpoint, files delivered in an AES-256 encrypted container (approved MoD key/certificate). File-format preferences: ISR imagery as GeoTIFF/JPEG2000 (high-res), sensor logs as timestamped CSV/TSV, forensic/damage assessments as signed PDF, HUMINT/detainee reports as redacted DOCX/PDF; include chain-of-custody metadata for each item. If SFTP is not available, prepare for a secure courier transfer. Please confirm: (A) FSB will attend at 14:00 Moscow, (B) FSB attendee list and names/roles, (C) provide the SFTP endpoint, receiving POC and key fingerprint (or courier pickup instructions), and (D) whether you want us to prioritize immediate delivery of forensic evidence and ISR imagery first, with HUMINT and full reports to follow.

FSB confirms attendance at the 14:00 Moscow planning session today and will join as requested. FSB attendee list (names/roles):
- Maj. Gen. Dmitri Sokolov — FSB Counterintelligence / Investigations Lead (session lead)
- Col. Aleksei Petrov — FSB Counterterrorism Operations
- Dr. Irina Mikhailova — Head, Technical Forensics / Blast Analysis
- Col. Viktor Lebedev — ISR Fusion / Imagery Analysis

Preferred secure transfer channel and delivery details (primary):
- SFTP over the classified network to the FSB secure ingest endpoint: sftp://fsb-secure-receive.internal (MoD-designated peering accepted). Receiving POC: Lt. Col. Elena Novikova; key fingerprint (SHA-256): 3A:7E:5C:9F:...:B2 (will verify on receipt). Use AES-256 encrypted containers; include chain-of-custody metadata and digital signatures for forensic items.
- Accepted file formats: ISR GeoTIFF/JPEG2000 (high-res), sensor logs CSV/TSV (timestamped, timezone noted), forensic/damage assessments signed PDF, HUMINT/detainee reports redacted DOCX/PDF. Metadata: geotags, timestamps, sensor/platform IDs, custody logs.
- Fallback: secure courier to FSB central evidence desk (provide pickup window and manifest in advance) if classified-SFTP is unavailable.

Prioritization guidance: prioritize immediate transmission of (1) on-site forensic evidence (signed chain-of-custody) and (2) highest-resolution ISR imagery and sensor logs for the bridge and nearby approaches — these are critical for attribution, target development, and arrest planning. HUMINT summaries and full reports may follow as they are cleared and redacted for joint dissemination. If you can stage delivery, send forensic items and ISR first, then HUMINT/detainee packages.

Request to Russian Armed Forces (action items for their message to FSB):
1) Confirm SFTP availability and confirm Lt. Col. Novikova's key fingerprint match or provide courier pickup window and contact. 2) Provide the RA attendee list with names/roles for 14:00 (so we can populate the agenda and information access authorities). 3) Confirm whether the 2-hour target for initial material delivery remains feasible; if not, provide an updated ETA and which items will be delivered first. 4) Flag any items requiring immediate operational hold or restrictions on dissemination.

FSB will deliver the written consolidated intelligence summary and formal threat assessment within the 12-hour window and will be prepared at 14:00 to task analytic and operational teams jointly upon receipt of the prioritized materials.

FSB — Confirming actions and details ahead of 14:00 Moscow session: 1) SFTP: Russian Armed Forces will use sftp://fsb-secure-receive.internal as primary ingest and will verify Lt. Col. Elena Novikova’s key fingerprint on connection. We will prioritize delivery in this order: (A) signed forensic packages with chain‑of‑custody, (B) highest‑resolution ISR imagery and sensor logs, (C) HUMINT/detainee summaries and full reports to follow as redaction/clearance permits. 4) Access/handling: no items require special operational hold beyond standard classified handling; flag any additional dissemination restrictions now. 5) Fallback: if classified‑SFTP is unavailable, propose secure courier pickup window 13:30–13:45 from MoD transfer point; MoD transfer POC: Lt. I will deliver an exact parts & munitions priority list in 30 minutes.

ISR / targeting (GUR/SBU action now): provide validated target coordinates and a single liaison cell; commit prioritized tactical UAV and SIGINT feeds to the Air Force for cueing and strike validation within the next 12 hours. SBU to assign protective detachments for battery movement and depot security now.

C2 & ROE: fuse civilian/military radar, AWACS/partner tracks and warning nets into one AD alert channel. Authorize delegated launch authority to named Air Force controllers when track quality meets the threshold I will publish in the 30‑minute package.

Risk mitigation: moving batteries will create temporary coverage gaps; mitigations are layered short‑range overlays, elevated CAP and prioritized ISR cueing. I will provide a map of residual coverage and expected protection effect (coverage/kill probability estimates) in the 45‑minute phased timeline.

Deliverables: parts/munitions priority list in 30 minutes; phased unit‑by‑unit redeployment timeline with maps and expected coverage effect in 45 minutes; nomination of Air Force HQ liaison within 10 minutes.

Request immediate confirmation of A–E now (or nomination of authorized delegates) so movement and sustainment actions may begin within the timelines above.

T+0 (within 10 minutes on approval): issue movement orders; nominate an Air Force HQ liaison to the joint C2 cell; assign SBU protective detachments to key sites; activate overtime maintenance teams and open 24‑hour field maintenance nodes at forward hubs.

T+0–2h (marshal & pre‑position): prepare Reserve Battery Alpha and Reserve Battery Bravo for forward movement; pre‑position 6 short‑range launcher platoons as temporary overlays at priority approach nodes; secure rail manifests and road convoy plans with military police escorts; task ISR: 2 ISR aircraft + 4 tactical UAVs to persistent loiter and begin SIGINT cueing to Air Force.

T+2–8h (movement & emplacement): execute rail/road moves; expected offload → site setup → initial IADS integration within 1–2 hours after offload; short‑range overlays and fighter CAP to cover transient gaps.

T+8h→sustain: layered coverage with medium‑range batteries primary, short‑range overlays and CAP filling gaps; CAP rotations 2h on/2h off, 4 fighters per high‑risk sector to maintain continuous presence and redeployment escort.

Immediate logistics & munitions asks (MoD action 6–12h): release for a 48‑hour surge — 240 medium‑range interceptors, 480 short‑range interceptors; release 200,000 L fuel and 6 spare engines; assign two transport brigades (one rail logistics brigade + one heavy‑lift road brigade) and priority rail/road corridors; establish two forward fuel & spares caches per hub. Господа, благодарю за письменную авторизацию. Подтверждаю получение и докладываю о дальнейших шагах: 

1) Москва немедленно приступает к активации муниципальных убежищ, введению целевых транспортных ограничений и мобилизации приоритетных аварийных бригад (энергетика, вода, связь, медицина). 

2) В течение 10 минут по защищённому каналу вышлю и одновременно пришлю копию в этот канал: а) полный список убежищ с адресами и координатами; б) детализованные данные по стационарам (текущая загрузка, число коек интенсивной помощи, аппаратов ИВЛ, контактные лица); в) расширенный контакт‑лист аварийных служб с резервными номерами и радиоканалами.

3) Прошу прислать по защищённому каналу/в этом канале: A) технические параметры защищённого канала (тип шифрования, адреса/учётные записи, контакт оператора/ответственного лица); B) официальный регламент медэвакуации и сопровождения колонн (форма запроса, максимальные сроки реакции, ответственные контакты, порядок подтверждения эскорта); C) формат и параметры передачи данных ПВО (координаты/сетка vs. адреса, приоритет сообщений) и контакт дежурного для прямой синхронизации. 

4) Доложим о ходе выполнения по каждому основному пункту в течение 30 минут и немедленно отправим через защищённый канал любые критические потребности. 

С уважением, Сергей Собянин, Мэр Москвы

data.content: Thank you for coming. We must coordinate EU and NATO support for Ukraine and strengthen alliance cohesion. I propose we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then agree on harmonized military, economic, and deterrence measures. Are you ready to begin?

Ready to begin. The EU proposes we proceed in three linked tracks: (A) a sanctions package focused on tighter export controls for dual‑use and advanced tech, targeted designations of senior officials/oligarchs and their networks, expanded financial measures (access to SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, asset freezes) and stepped‑up enforcement; (B) targeted financial assistance for Ukraine combining immediate budget support/grants, credit guarantees to stabilise banking, and a reconstruction/resilience facility with strict oversight and delivery channels; (C) candidate‑country status decisions handled on their merits but with coordinated political messaging. I suggest we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then set up a NATO–EU working group to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging, with a proposed timeline for deliverables. Do you agree to begin with brief updates now?

Draft coordinated reply for signature: Thank you, Jens — we fully agree coordination is essential. The EU proposes the following immediate steps and asks NATO to confirm priorities and co‑lead where indicated. 1) Begin brief updates now from each side on assistance priorities (military support needs, urgent civilian/budget gaps, macro‑financial risks). 2) Sanctions track (EU take lead, NATO to share targeting/impact intelligence): adopt tighter export controls on dual‑use and advanced technologies; move to targeted designations of senior officials, oligarchs and enablers and their networks; expand financial measures including SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, targeted asset freezes and secondary‑measures to limit circumvention; and step up enforcement cooperation (information‑sharing, joint investigations). 3) Financial assistance track (EU lead on instruments, ask NATO to coordinate resilience/logistics support): immediate budget support grants and emergency liquidity guarantees to stabilise Ukraine’s public finances and banking sector; a reconstruction/resilience facility combining grants, concessional lending and strict oversight; credit guarantees and risk sharing with partners to unlock private finance; clear fiduciary controls and delivery channels to ensure rapid, accountable disbursement. 4) Candidate‑country status coordination: handle accession decisions on their merits but align political messaging to preserve regional cohesion and deterrence. 5) Institutional follow‑up: establish a NATO–EU working group (co‑chaired EU Political/External Action and NATO Policy) to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, design joint financial instruments, and coordinate deterrence messaging. Proposed near‑term timeline: consolidated priorities and shared sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; an operational enforcement-sharing protocol within 1 month; a draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days. Please confirm NATO’s readiness to (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting/intel for sanctions, and (c) co‑chair the working group. Are you ready to begin with the brief updates?

data.content: Thank you for coming. We must coordinate EU and NATO support for Ukraine and strengthen alliance cohesion. I propose we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then agree on harmonized military, economic, and deterrence measures. Are you ready to begin?

Ready to begin. The EU proposes we proceed in three linked tracks: (A) a sanctions package focused on tighter export controls for dual‑use and advanced tech, targeted designations of senior officials/oligarchs and their networks, expanded financial measures (access to SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, asset freezes) and stepped‑up enforcement; (B) targeted financial assistance for Ukraine combining immediate budget support/grants, credit guarantees to stabilise banking, and a reconstruction/resilience facility with strict oversight and delivery channels; (C) candidate‑country status decisions handled on their merits but with coordinated political messaging. I suggest we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then set up a NATO–EU working group to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging, with a proposed timeline for deliverables. Do you agree to begin with brief updates now?

Draft coordinated reply for signature: Thank you, Jens — we fully agree coordination is essential. The EU proposes the following immediate steps and asks NATO to confirm priorities and co‑lead where indicated. 1) Begin brief updates now from each side on assistance priorities (military support needs, urgent civilian/budget gaps, macro‑financial risks). 2) Sanctions track (EU take lead, NATO to share targeting/impact intelligence): adopt tighter export controls on dual‑use and advanced technologies; move to targeted designations of senior officials, oligarchs and enablers and their networks; expand financial measures including SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, targeted asset freezes and secondary‑measures to limit circumvention; and step up enforcement cooperation (information‑sharing, joint investigations). 3) Financial assistance track (EU lead on instruments, ask NATO to coordinate resilience/logistics support): immediate budget support grants and emergency liquidity guarantees to stabilise Ukraine’s public finances and banking sector; a reconstruction/resilience facility combining grants, concessional lending and strict oversight; credit guarantees and risk sharing with partners to unlock private finance; clear fiduciary controls and delivery channels to ensure rapid, accountable disbursement. 4) Candidate‑country status coordination: handle accession decisions on their merits but align political messaging to preserve regional cohesion and deterrence. 5) Institutional follow‑up: establish a NATO–EU working group (co‑chaired EU Political/External Action and NATO Policy) to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, design joint financial instruments, and coordinate deterrence messaging. Proposed near‑term timeline: consolidated priorities and shared sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; an operational enforcement-sharing protocol within 1 month; a draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days. Please confirm NATO’s readiness to (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting/intel for sanctions, and (c) co‑chair the working group. Are you ready to begin with the brief updates?

Thank you — NATO fully endorses the EU’s three‑track approach and agrees that close NATO–EU coordination is essential. NATO is ready to: (a) give immediate brief updates now on urgent military assistance priorities (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training) and on eastern‑flank reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped‑up ISR); (b) share targeting and intelligence to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement; and (c) co‑chair the proposed NATO–EU working group (NATO Policy with EU Political/External Action) to draft harmonised measures, pooled funding options and an enforcement‑sharing protocol. EU one‑page brief — urgent financial & budget needs for Ukraine (summary)

1) Immediate fiscal gap (next 3 months): estimated €5–7bn to cover public payrolls, social benefits, energy subsidies and essential public services. Request: immediate budget support grants to bridge cash shortfalls and avoid public service collapse.

2) Liquidity and banking stability: urgent liquidity support and emergency credit guarantees to shore up banks and restore market confidence. Proposal: a €10bn risk‑sharing/guarantee envelope (EU + partners + IFIs) to unlock short‑term lending and central bank liquidity lines.

3) Emergency social and energy assistance: targeted grants for heating/fuel, critical health supplies, and municipal services to prevent humanitarian collapse this winter.

4) Reconstruction & resilience facility: create a pipeline of priority quick‑start projects (energy grid repair, ports/logistics, hospitals, water/sewer, transport nodes). Facility should combine grants, concessional loans, and blended finance with strict fiduciary controls and rapid disbursement windows.

5) Delivery, oversight and safeguards: single EU‑managed fiduciary channel for rapid payments; clear procurement safeguards, AML/CFT screening, independent audits and public reporting; on‑the‑ground delivery partners pre‑cleared to speed rollout.

6) Mobilising private capital: propose credit enhancements, first‑loss tranches and donor co‑investment to crowd in institutional investors for reconstruction bonds.

7) Coordination asks of NATO/Allies: confirm logistics/resilience support (secure corridors, naval/airlift slots, escorts for critical shipments), liaison for procurement/delivery timelines, and ability to coordinate protection of critical infrastructure shipments.

Кратко и по пунктам — моё приоритетное решение: опция 1 — оборонительная консолидация и стабилизация тылов.
1) Немедленные общие распоряжения (для штабов и Черноморского флота): привести в повышенную готовность подразделения обороны, сосредоточить усилия на восстановлении запасов и логистических линий, усилить средства ПВО и РЭБ, обеспечить защиту критической инфраструктуры и тыловых узлов коммуникаций; Черноморскому флоту — поддержка мер по контролю морских коммуникаций и готовность к задачам обеспечения и реакции. 
2) Требуемые силы и средства (категории): дополнительные боеприпасы и материально‑технические резервы; пополнение личного состава и ротация резервов; усиленные подразделения ПВО и средства радиотехнической борьбы; авиационные и морские ресурсы на уровне оперативного распределения; возможности разведки и целеуказания. 
3) Ключевые риски: продолжение ударов по гражданской инфраструктуре, наращивание западных поставок и возможная эскалация на смежных направлениях; эти риски требуют приоритетных мер ПВО и дипломатической координации. 
4) Сроки: стабилизация и консолидация — ориентир 2–4 недели; параллельная подготовка ограниченной наступательной опции — ориентир 6–8 недель при подтверждённой готовности. 
Прошу санкционировать приоритет на оборонную консолидацию и дать полномочия штабу на формирование конкретных заявок по категориям и срокам; по вашему разрешению я немедленно представлю детализированную сводку потребностей и картографические материалы в закрытом порядке.

data.content: General Zaluzhnyi, thank you for joining me. I want to discuss Ukraine's operational needs and how the United Kingdom can best support them. What are your immediate priorities, and which capabilities do you need most from us?

Admiral Radakin — thank you. My immediate operational priorities are:

1) Air defence: integrated medium‑ and long‑range AD systems, interceptors, munitions and sustainment to protect population centers, critical infrastructure and forward units.
2) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires: missiles, guided rockets and targeting support to interdict Russian logistics, command nodes and long‑range launch systems.
3) Artillery and ammunition: steady deliveries of 155mm rounds, additional tubes/MLRS and maintenance support to sustain offensive and defensive operations.
4) ISR, EW and air surveillance: timely satellite/AWACS coverage, SIGINT/IMINT sharing and EW capabilities to improve battlespace awareness and force protection.
5) Logistics, engineering and mobility: bridging, heavy lift, fuel, depot and repair support to maintain operational tempo.
6) Personnel and sustainment: UK training teams, maintenance crews and liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed integration and readiness.

Timing: air defence and ammunition resupply are urgent (weeks); building deep‑strike stockpiles and sustainment capacity is critical over the coming months. Please advise what the UK can deliver in the near term and what NATO political/security measures you can mobilize (airspace coordination, basing, accelerated approvals, sanctions alignment). I propose a UK technical delegation meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv within days to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. I can send a prioritized list with quantities immediately. Thank you.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you for that clear, prioritised briefing. We will treat air defence and 155mm ammunition resupply as the immediate UK priorities. In the near term (weeks) the UK can accelerate deliveries of AD munitions and 155mm rounds from available stocks, expedite export and mobilisation approvals, and task logistics and maintenance teams to sustain incoming systems and ammunition. We welcome and accept your proposal for a UK technical delegation to meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. Please send your prioritized list with quantities, preferred systems/interfaces and any lift or basing constraints as soon as possible, and propose available dates for the Kyiv meeting. On the political/security side I will immediately raise coordination with NATO and our partners on airspace deconfliction, basing options and accelerated approvals/sanctions alignment to speed delivery and sustainment. I will prioritise getting a small UK technical team to Kyiv within days once we have your list and dates. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — thank you. Below is Ukraine’s prioritized list (high‑level quantities, preferred systems/interfaces, and lift/basing constraints) for immediate UK technical planning:

1) Air defence (urgent — weeks): 2 long‑range AD batteries (Patriot or equivalent) with initial launcher elements and ~200 interceptors; 6 medium‑range AD systems (NASAMS / IRIS‑T SLM or equivalent) with ~600 interceptors; sustainment spares, IFF/C2 integration (Link‑16 capable), training teams and maintenance detachments. Lift: strategic airlift for systems, routine sealift/road for munitions.

2) 155mm artillery & ammunition (urgent — weeks): total request 200,000 rounds over 3 months, staged deliveries (50k within 4 weeks, 75k within 8 weeks, 75k within 12 weeks). Also request ~100 155mm tubes (mix of towed and SP) and maintenance crews. Lift: sealift + strategic airlift for urgent batches.

3) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires (critical — months): 200–300 precision long‑range munitions (ATACMS/Storm Shadow class or equivalent) with associated targeting assets (UAV designation pods, targeting cell access) and sustainment spares. Requires secure build‑up and secure transport corridors.

4) ISR, EW & air surveillance (high): prioritized satellite tasking, one AWACS rotation commitment, continuous SIGINT/IMINT feeds, and four EW detachments with integration support to fuse into Ukrainian C2.

5) Logistics, engineering & mobility: heavy‑lift / bridging assets, fuel depot stockpiles, forward repair hubs, and UK logistics teams to establish sustainment nodes closer to the front.

6) Personnel & sustainment: deploy 4–6 UK technical/training teams (12–20 personnel each), maintenance crews, and 6–8 liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed system integration and sustainment.

Basing / transport constraints: immediate munitions and spares should flow into allied hubs (Poland/Romania/other) for onward road/rail; long‑range systems need secure airlift and space for integration/testing. We require expedited export approvals, airspace deconfliction for transit, and temporary basing/access where necessary.

Proposed Kyiv meeting: UK technical delegation to Kyiv within 3–5 days. Proposed options: Option A — earliest (in 3 days); Option B — in 5 days. Please confirm your team’s earliest availability and which specialists you will include (AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance). On confirmation I will send a line‑item prioritized list with exact quantities, preferred system variants/interfaces and emplacement/lift requirements for planners.

Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — to finalise the Kyiv meeting please confirm: 1) which option you prefer (Option A — in 3 days; Option B — in 5 days) and your earliest arrival date; 2) team composition (specialists and numbers: AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance, others); and 3) any security, basing or airport/hub support you will require from Ukrainian side. On receipt I will coordinate Ukrainian staff, logistics and provide the detailed line‑item list for planners.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. We confirm Option A: a UK technical delegation will aim to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days (earliest availability). Proposed initial team composition (subject to final adjustment once we receive your line‑item list):

• AD specialists — 6 personnel (systems integration, IFF/Link‑16/C2, operator trainers)
• Munitions & logistics planners — 6 personnel (ammunition planners, strategic/operational lift coordinators)
• C2/EW specialists — 4 personnel (EW integration officers, SIGINT/IMINT liaisons)
• Maintenance detachments — 8 personnel (engineers/technicians for AD and artillery systems)
• Command & liaison — 2 senior officers

Approx. total: ~26 personnel. On support we require from Ukrainian side: secure air corridor/airspace deconfliction to the agreed airfield (Boryspil or alternative), priority handling and customs facilitation for team and urgent equipment, secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection/ground security for personnel and equipment while in Kyiv, and access to allied hubs (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging. Please confirm Option A and the availability of the requested security/basing/hub support and I will issue flight manifests, exact team rosters and equipment lists within 24 hours of your confirmation and on receipt of the detailed line‑item list. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — confirmed. We accept Option A: the UK technical delegation to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days. Ukraine will provide the requested support: airspace deconfliction to the agreed airfield (Boryspil preferred unless you advise otherwise), priority handling and customs facilitation, a secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection/ground security for personnel and equipment while in Kyiv, and access to allied hubs (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging. Ukrainian staff will coordinate reception, secure integration facilities and fast‑track customs and hub movement. Please send flight manifests, the exact team roster and full equipment lists within 24 hours so we can finalise security, ground handling and hub arrangements. Also confirm your preferred airfield and estimated arrival time. Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Кратко: переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения о вывозе зерна сорваны — я покинул встречу. Сразу после этого украинские южные порты подверглись новой волне блокирующих артобстрелов; практическая реализация соглашения фактически приостановлена. Прошу подтверждения на подготовку заявления и поручения Минобороны к выработке конкретных опций.

Переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения о вывозе зерна сорваны; после моего ухода украинские южные порты подверглись новой волне артобстрелов — экспорт фактически приостановлен. Рекомендации: 1) одобрить оперативное заявление (Песков зачтёт); 2) усилить морские и береговые патрули, временно приостановить совместные инспекции до гарантий безопасности коридоров; 3) направить дипломатические ноты Турции и ООН с требованием деэскалации; 4) поручить Минобороны подготовить варианты оперативного реагирования и меры по защите экспортной инфраструктуры. Прошу распоряжений.

Mr. President, Ministers, Colleagues — I will give a short briefing on Moscow's security and civil‑defence readiness and request immediate coordination of municipal measures. Current posture: Moscow city services are on high alert and standing by; emergency crews, medical teams and municipal utilities are being prepared for rapid deployment; shelter and medical capacity is being readied city‑wide. I request your immediate authorization to: (a) coordinate air/ground security and situation awareness with the General Staff and Ministry of Defence; (b) activate civil‑defence measures, open designated shelters, and implement targeted transport restrictions where required; (c) mobilize municipal emergency teams and priority crews for power, water and communications resilience; (d) release clear public instructions via the Kremlin press office and faith/community channels to prevent panic. I ask for guidance and authorization to execute these measures now.

Ваше обращение принято. Прошу Генеральный штаб и Минобороны немедленно согласовать режим безопасного прекращения огня на 6–7 января и меры охраны для обеспечения безопасности верующих и храмов. Прошу Минобороны координироваться с московскими муниципальными службами (господин Собянин) по организации безопасного прибытия в храмы, открытию необходимых укрытий и обеспечению работы аварийных и коммунальных служб. Пресс‑службе Кремля поручаю подготовить и выпустить ясные публичные инструкции, согласованные с церковными каналами. Прошу Минобороны и Генштаб представить конкретные оперативные рекомендации и предложения по безопасности прямо в конференц-зале — немедленно.

Принято. Немедленно направляюсь в конференц‑зал Кремля и прошу всех присутствующих присоединиться. Коротко — підсумок від Podolyak: нічні удари БПЛА по Дніпропетровській, Миколаївській, Запорізькій і Херсонській областях; підтверджено 2 поранених (Запоріжжя, Кривий Ріг); оцінки пошкоджень та походження уламків у роботі.

Президент авторизував негайну реалізацію пунктів 1 і 4 (підвищення постур ППО та тимчасове перерозподілення мобільних ППО на південь; активація укриттів і розгортання мед/гуманітарних команд). Інші пункти тримати в режимі готовності.

Негайні маршрутизація/накази (підтвердити можливість і ETA в 10–15 хв):
- Mykhailo Podolyak: розіслати повні звіти про пошкодження й цільову розвідку в цей зал, регіональним координаторам, Andriy Yermak і Government of Ukraine протягом 60 хв — надсилайте після підтверджень.
- Andriy Yermak / Government: підготувати єдине коротке зовнішнє повідомлення і оперативні запити партнерам (Brussels/Washington); винести фінальний текст у залі для погодження (ETA 30–60 хв).
- Pavlo Kyrylenko: зібрати секторні SITREP (Київ, Північ, Схід, Південь, Захід) і надати до цієї зали протягом 10–15 хв.
- Mykola Oleshchuk: підвищити постур ППО і почати тимчасове перерозподілення мобільних засобів на південь; вкажіть ETA на перекидання.
- Oleksandr Syrskyi / MoD: підготувати варіанти перехоплення/контрзаходів з юридичною оцінкою; вкажіть ETA на готовність.
- Kyrylo Budanov / GUR / SBU: почати судово‑технічне вилучення уламків і аналіз походження, призначити ліаїзонів до MoD; підтвердьте можливість та ETA.
- Ihor Klymenko / Police / Vitali Klitschko: активувати укриття, захистити критичну інфраструктуру, розгорнути медичні і гуманітарні резерви; підтвердьте ETA.

Усім: підтвердьте можливість виконання і надайте ETA на першочергові заходи (10–15 хв). Podolyak — після підтвердження розсилайте повні матеріали в зал, регіони і Yermak/Government; пункти 1 і 4 можна виконувати зараз.

EU one‑page brief — urgent financial & budget needs for Ukraine (summary)

1) Immediate fiscal gap (next 3 months): estimated €5–7bn to cover public payrolls, social benefits, energy subsidies and essential public services. Request: immediate budget support grants to bridge cash shortfalls and avoid public service collapse.

2) Liquidity and banking stability: urgent liquidity support and emergency credit guarantees to shore up banks and restore market confidence. Proposal: a €10bn risk‑sharing/guarantee envelope (EU + partners + IFIs) to unlock short‑term lending and central bank liquidity lines.

3) Emergency social and energy assistance: targeted grants for heating/fuel, critical health supplies, and municipal services to prevent humanitarian collapse this winter.

4) Reconstruction & resilience facility: create a pipeline of priority quick‑start projects (energy grid repair, ports/logistics, hospitals, water/sewer, transport nodes). Facility should combine grants, concessional loans, and blended finance with strict fiduciary controls and rapid disbursement windows.

5) Delivery, oversight and safeguards: single EU‑managed fiduciary channel for rapid payments; clear procurement safeguards, AML/CFT screening, independent audits and public reporting; on‑the‑ground delivery partners pre‑cleared to speed rollout.

6) Mobilising private capital: propose credit enhancements, first‑loss tranches and donor co‑investment to crowd in institutional investors for reconstruction bonds.

7) Coordination asks of NATO/Allies: confirm logistics/resilience support (secure corridors, naval/airlift slots, escorts for critical shipments), liaison for procurement/delivery timelines, and ability to coordinate protection of critical infrastructure shipments.

1) Немедленные общие распоряжения (для штабов и Черноморского флота): привести в повышенную готовность подразделения обороны, сосредоточить усилия на восстановлении запасов и логистических линий, усилить средства ПВО и РЭБ, обеспечить защиту критической инфраструктуры и тыловых узлов коммуникаций; Черноморскому флоту — поддержка мер по контролю морских коммуникаций и готовность к задачам обеспечения и реакции. 
2) Требуемые силы и средства (категории): дополнительные боеприпасы и материально‑технические резервы; пополнение личного состава и ротация резервов; усиленные подразделения ПВО и средства радиотехнической борьбы; авиационные и морские ресурсы на уровне оперативного распределения; возможности разведки и целеуказания. 
3) Ключевые риски: продолжение ударов по гражданской инфраструктуре, наращивание западных поставок и возможная эскалация на смежных направлениях; эти риски требуют приоритетных мер ПВО и дипломатической координации. 
4) Сроки: стабилизация и консолидация — ориентир 2–4 недели; параллельная подготовка ограниченной наступательной опции — ориентир 6–8 недель при подтверждённой готовности. 
Прошу санкционировать приоритет на оборонную консолидацию и дать полномочия штабу на формирование конкретных заявок по категориям и срокам; по вашему разрешению я немедленно представлю детализированную сводку потребностей и картографические материалы в закрытом порядке.

市长，已收到并记录您的详报。为便于我方立即对接中央并启动调配，请以简短条目尽快确认下列可量化信息并给出现场联络人：

1) “莫斯科号”精确位置（码头名称/泊位或近海坐标）；是否可靠泊入坞或需拖带？推进/动力是否可用？主要损伤部位？预计入坞开始时间窗与完工估计（最优/典型/最差，天数）。

2) 干船坞/浮船坞与拖带：目前可用干/浮坞清单（每座最大承载/船长/吃水），可用拖轮数量与最大拖带能力；优先需调入的类型与最早可用时间。

3) 起重与修理能力：现有重型起重机台数及单台能力（吨）；缺口需补多少台；现有维修人员/班组数量与能到岗的最早时间；紧急关键备件清单与短缺数量（发动机/推进、雷达/通信件等）。

4) 弹药与燃油库存：主要弹药（反舰、对空、舰炮）与燃油现有量、估算可支撑天数及短缺量。

5) 防空与EW现状与缺口：已部署的远程/中程/近程防空系统及数量（S‑400/S‑300/Pantsir/CIWS/机动短程/MANPADS）、EW与反无人系统现存数量与部署空缺；建议补充数量与优先级。

6) 港区与水域安全：计划或可立即执行的扫雷/航道排查时间窗，现有扫雷与护航编队规模，可用拖轮与泊位重排方案；请按优先时限（24–72小时 / 数日 / 数周）标注每项措施的可行性。

data.content: Request current strategic posture update and coordination on next steps. Please provide a consolidated intelligence summary, threat assessment, and recommended priorities for joint action. Propose convening a brief joint planning session to align posture and responsibilities—when can FSB attend?

FSB acknowledges request. We will prepare a consolidated intelligence summary, threat assessment, and recommended priorities for joint action. Proposed timeline: deliver written summary within 12 hours. Recommend a brief joint planning session at 14:00 Moscow time today or 09:00 tomorrow — confirm preferred time and list of attendees. Immediately provide to FSB: (1) latest ISR imagery and sensor logs for the Crimean Bridge area, (2) results of on-site forensic teams and damage assessment, (3) any detained suspects or leads from HUMINT, and (4) reports of foreign signatures or unusual capabilities observed. FSB will task analytic and operational teams to coordinate identification and arrest actions upon receipt of those materials and will attend at the confirmed time.

Preliminary strategic posture update (FSB → Russian Armed Forces):

Intelligence summary (initial):
- Crimean Bridge sustained significant damage; on-site forensic teams and damage assessment are still reporting — FSB has not yet received complete forensics or ISR package. 
- No definitive attribution at this time; current reporting includes unverified indicators of external involvement and unusual signatures that require technical analysis. 
- Available reporting indicates elevated activity in the wider theater and related strikes/retaliatory fires; casualty and infrastructure-impact figures remain being confirmed.

Threat assessment (initial):
- High risk of follow-on attacks or sabotage against the bridge and supporting logistics nodes while damage remains unmitigated. 
- Elevated risk of escalation and asymmetric attacks (maritime drones, loitering munitions, remote sabotage). 
- Operational environment favors rapid intelligence collection and interdiction to prevent further incidents and to preserve forensic evidence for attribution and legal/operational follow-up.

Recommended immediate priorities (FSB recommends these as joint actions):
1) Secure and cordon the bridge and all access routes to preserve forensics and prevent secondary incidents. 
2) Centralize ISR (satellite, aerial, maritime, electronic) and sensor logs into a single analytic tasking node; prioritize high-resolution imagery of the bridge, approaches, and likely staging areas.
3) Expedite forensic triage and chain-of-custody reporting; provide technical signatures (explosive/munition, blast pattern, command-and-control traces) to counterintelligence and technical analysis teams. 
4) Generate and circulate vetted HUMINT leads and detainee reports to the joint task node; prioritize interviewing and evidence linkage. 
5) Harden nearby logistics and transit nodes, increase patrols (maritime/air/ground) and border screening for unusual movements. 
6) Prepare legal/diplomatic briefings and information operations to manage escalation and public messaging.

Operational request to Russian Armed Forces (repeat/clarify): immediately transmit to FSB: (1) latest ISR imagery and sensor logs covering the Crimean Bridge and approaches, (2) complete on-site forensic and damage-assessment reports, (3) list and status of any detained suspects and HUMINT leads, and (4) any technical reports of foreign signatures or unusual capabilities observed. Receipt of these materials will allow FSB to finalize attribution analysis and operational targeting for arrests.

Coordination/meeting: FSB reiterates written consolidated intelligence summary and formal threat assessment will be delivered within 12 hours. We propose a brief joint planning session to align posture and responsibilities — preferred time: 14:00 Moscow today; alternate: 09:00 Moscow tomorrow. Please confirm the chosen time and provide a short attendee list (suggested attendees: Russian Armed Forces operational command representative, FSB counterterrorism/investigations lead, GRU liaison, Investigative Committee, Border Guards, Ministry of Transport/crimea administration representative, and the forensic/technical lead).

FSB stands ready to task analytic and operational teams to coordinate identification, arrest, and follow-on actions upon receipt of the requested materials and at the confirmed planning session.

Acknowledged. We prefer the 14:00 Moscow session today. Proposed Russian Armed Forces attendees: Deputy Minister of Defense (Operations), Chief of Joint Operations, GRU liaison, Head ISR, Chief of Logistics, Lead Forensic Officer. We will compile and deliver the requested materials for the Crimean Bridge: (1) latest ISR imagery and sensor logs, (2) on-site forensic and damage-assessment reports, (3) detained suspects and HUMINT leads, (4) reports of any foreign signatures or unusual capabilities. Target delivery of these materials within 2 hours. Please confirm: (A) you will attend at 14:00 Moscow, (B) your list of attendees, and (C) preferred secure transfer channel and file/encryption requirements (SFTP over classified network, secure courier, format specifications). Any further prioritization guidance for analytic/operational tasks?

Confirmed: Russian Armed Forces will attend the 14:00 Moscow planning session today. Proposed RA attendees (final): Deputy Minister of Defense (Operations), Chief of Joint Operations, GRU liaison, Head ISR, Chief of Logistics, Lead Forensic Officer. We will deliver the requested materials within 2 hours. Preferred transfer: SFTP over the classified network to an MoD-designated endpoint, files delivered in an AES-256 encrypted container (approved MoD key/certificate). File-format preferences: ISR imagery as GeoTIFF/JPEG2000 (high-res), sensor logs as timestamped CSV/TSV, forensic/damage assessments as signed PDF, HUMINT/detainee reports as redacted DOCX/PDF; include chain-of-custody metadata for each item. If SFTP is not available, prepare for a secure courier transfer. Please confirm: (A) FSB will attend at 14:00 Moscow, (B) FSB attendee list and names/roles, (C) provide the SFTP endpoint, receiving POC and key fingerprint (or courier pickup instructions), and (D) whether you want us to prioritize immediate delivery of forensic evidence and ISR imagery first, with HUMINT and full reports to follow.

FSB confirms attendance at the 14:00 Moscow planning session today and will join as requested. FSB attendee list (names/roles):
- Maj. Gen. Dmitri Sokolov — FSB Counterintelligence / Investigations Lead (session lead)
- Col. Aleksei Petrov — FSB Counterterrorism Operations
- Dr. Irina Mikhailova — Head, Technical Forensics / Blast Analysis

- SFTP over the classified network to the FSB secure ingest endpoint: sftp://fsb-secure-receive.internal (MoD-designated peering accepted). Receiving POC: Lt. Col. Elena Novikova; key fingerprint (SHA-256): 3A:7E:5C:9F:...:B2 (will verify on receipt). Use AES-256 encrypted containers; include chain-of-custody metadata and digital signatures for forensic items.

HUMINT summaries and full reports may follow as they are cleared and redacted for joint dissemination. If you can stage delivery, send forensic items and ISR first, then HUMINT/detainee packages.

Господин Президент, господин Министр: по вашей просьбе — кратко и по пунктам.

Приоритет: опция 1 — оборонительная консолидация и стабилизация тылов.

Немедленные обобщённые распоряжения (без тактических указаний): штабу — провести оперативную проверку наличных МТО и представить сводные заявки по ключевым категориям (боеприпасы, горюче‑смазочные материалы, запасы связи и медобеспечения), организовать ротацию и пополнение личного состава в наиболее перегруженных участках; усилить интеграцию ПВО и средств РЭБ для прикрытия тылов и важной инфраструктуры. Черноморскому флоту — усилить контроль морских коммуникаций и подготовить силы для задач морского обеспечения и реагирования на угрозы на море. (Детализация — в закрытом докладе.)

Требуемые силы и средства — по категориям: пополнение боеприпасов и МТО; пополнение и ротация личного состава; усиление средств ПВО и РЭБ; возможности разведки и целеуказания; ресурсы для защиты критической инфраструктуры.

Ключевые риски: удары по гражданской и энергетической инфраструктуре; наращивание внешних поставок противника; вероятность эскалации на смежных направлениях. Необходимы приоритетные меры ПВО, РЭБ и дипломатическая координация.

Сроки: стабилизация и консолидация — ориентир 2–4 недели; параллельная подготовка ограниченной наступательной опции — ориентир 6–8 недель при подтверждённой готовности.

data.content: We are convening an urgent security briefing now. President Zelenskyy, Ministry of Defence, SBU, GUR, and frontline commanders: please take your seats. Ministry of Defence and commanders — give a 5‑minute operational update on the frontline. GUR and SBU — report latest intelligence and internal‑security issues. Kyrylo Budanov — present key intelligence priorities. Secure communications. Begin now.

Mr President, Minister, chiefs — brief from Ukrainian Air Force: readiness is high with air-defence and fighter units on alert. Recent successful actions include the downing of a Russian Su-34 (21 Feb 2024) and high interception performance during recent missile waves (e.g., 72 of 99 missiles reported intercepted on 2024-01-02). Immediate proposals for adjustment: 1) concentrate mobile SAM batteries and additional short-range launchers to reinforce Kyiv and Kharkiv sectors and critical airports; 2) increase persistent fighter CAP over likely approach corridors during high-alert hours; 3) reallocate AD ammunition resupplies and request urgent ISR/tactical UAV assets to pre-locate launch clusters; 4) coordinate with SBU/GUR to prioritise strikes on launch and command nodes. Request approval now to re-task assets and to seek expedited logistic support from MOD and Government.

Mr President, Minister, Chiefs — brief follow-up and immediate execution plan if I have your authority now:

1) Immediate re-tasking (start within 2 hours on approval): concentrate all available mobile SAM batteries and short-range launchers into a layered arc protecting Kyiv, Kharkiv and the nation's principal international airports; temporarily pull two reserve SAM batteries from lower-risk southern sectors and forward-deploy them by rail/road with military police escort. Increase persistent fighter CAP over the most-likely approach corridors in the north‑east and toward Kyiv during peak threat hours (set CAP rotations to 2-hour on / 2-hour off to sustain presence without exceeding pilot flight-hour limits).

2) Firepower & logistics demands (need MOD/Government action within 6–12 hours): prioritize immediate re-supply of AD interceptors and launcher munitions from central depots; release fuel and spare-engines earmarked as reserves; allocate two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) and priority road corridors to move batteries and launchers. We will publish a parts/munitions priority list within 30 minutes — request expedited approval to draw and distribute those stocks.

3) ISR and targeting (request to GUR/SBU now): assign prioritized tactical UAVs and ISR aircraft to persistent loiter over suspected launch areas; grant the Air Force direct feeds and coordinates for credible clusters so we can cue SAMs and fighters. Request SBU/GUR target validation for strike tasking on identified launch nodes within 12 hours so strike assets can be coordinated.

4) C2 and warnings: elevate AD C2 to high tempo — fuse civilian/military radar, AWACS/partner tracks, and national missile-warning nets into a single alert channel; clear rules to allow fast hand-off to interceptors under delegated authority when track quality meets threshold.

5) Personnel & maintenance: authorize overtime maintenance teams and immediate rotation of crews to sustain higher sortie and launcher tempo; establish a 24‑hour field maintenance node at the forward redeployment hubs.

6) Risk mitigation & phasing: we will prioritize protection of population centers and critical infrastructure first, industrial/secondary sectors second; moving batteries creates temporary coverage gaps — we will mitigate with fighter CAP and short-range launcher overlays. I will consolidate a phased redeployment plan in 45 minutes showing exact timelines and units moved.

Requests for decisions now: (A) approval to re-task and forward-deploy the named mobile SAM batteries and to reassign two reserve batteries from the south; (B) approval for MOD/Government to release prioritized AD munitions and transport assets; (C) SBU/GUR commitment to provide validated target coordinates and ISR priority. With your approval we will begin execution immediately and I will report back with the redeployment timeline and expected effect within one hour.

Understood, Mr President. I will hold my detailed damage and port-report until after General Syrskyi's operational brief. Quick coordination points from the Air Force now: 1) We will produce the phased redeployment plan and exact unit/timeline within 45 minutes and the parts & munitions priority list within 30 minutes. 2) Request immediate MOD approval to re-task two reserve mobile SAM batteries from the southern sectors and to assign two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) with priority corridors for forward movement. 3) Request expedited release of AD interceptors, launcher munitions, fuel, and spare engines per our priority list. 4) Request SBU/GUR to assign a single validated-target liaison and grant the Air Force direct ISR/tactical UAV feeds for cueing within the next 12 hours. 5) I will nominate an Air Force HQ liaison officer to the joint C2 cell now to coordinate redeployment and sustainment. With your approval of those authorizations we will begin execution immediately and report back with the redeployment timeline within one hour.

Mr President, Minister, Chiefs — concise frontline air‑defence plan and immediate requests for authority to execute now:

1) Immediate deployments (start within 2 hours on approval): concentrate available mobile medium‑range SAM batteries and short‑range launcher clusters into a layered arc protecting Kyiv and Kharkiv plus the nation’s principal international airports. Forward‑deploy two reserve mobile SAM batteries from lower‑risk southern sectors by rail/road with military police escort. Establish short‑range launcher overlays at key approach nodes while medium‑range batteries move.

2) Fighter CAP (effective immediately on approval): increase persistent CAP over likely approach corridors with 2‑hour on / 2‑hour off rotations to sustain presence without exceeding pilot flight‑hour ceilings; prioritize armed escort of redeployments and temporary coverage of gaps.

3) Logistics & munitions (MOD action needed within 6–12 hours): priority release of AD interceptors and launcher munitions sufficient to sustain high‑tempo defence for the next 48 hours; release earmarked fuel and spare engines; allocate two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) and priority road/rail corridors for battery movement. I will send an exact parts & munitions priority list in 30 minutes and a phased redeployment timeline in 45 minutes.

4) ISR & targeting (GUR/SBU action now): assign prioritized tactical UAVs, ISR aircraft, and SIGINT leads to persistent loiter over suspected launch areas and provide direct, validated coordinate feeds to the Air Force. Request a single validated‑target liaison from GUR/SBU and legal clearance to circulate targetable intel to MoD/GUR/strike planners within the hour.

5) C2 & rules of engagement: elevate AD C2 to high tempo—fuse civilian and military radar, AWACS/partner tracks and national warning nets into a single alert channel. Authorize delegated launch authority to named Air Force controllers for fast hand‑off when track quality meets the established threshold (I will provide the threshold parameters in the redeployment timeline).

- Liaison: embed SBU liaison cells with MoD, GUR, MVS, and regional administrations for real‑time coordination and strike/vulnerability deconfliction.

- Messaging support: SBU will provide vetted talking points for Presidential/Head‑of‑Office use and produce a one‑page intelligence annex for Brussels/Washington delegations.

Asks now: authorize synchronized warrants and simultaneous operations; approve temporary enhanced protective measures for air‑defence sites; endorse 30‑day martial‑law extension as requested to enable swift law‑enforcement action. SBU ready to lead and execute immediately; request operational go/no‑go and legal clearances now.

1) Forensic recovery & origin analysis (Podolyak item 2): SBU will launch joint forensic debris‑recovery teams with GUR immediately. Teams and equipment are being readied now; we can task and nominate SBU liaisons to MoD within 30 minutes. Field recovery teams can deploy to prioritized sites (Dnipro/Kherson/Mykolaiv/Zaporizhzhia) within ~2 hours, subject to MoD clearance for ISZ entry; request Syrskyi confirm safe‑work windows and escort availability.
