Admiral Radakin — thank you. My immediate operational priorities are:

1) Air defence: integrated medium‑ and long‑range AD systems, interceptors, munitions and sustainment to protect population centers, critical infrastructure and forward units.
2) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires: missiles, guided rockets and targeting support to interdict Russian logistics, command nodes and long‑range launch systems.
3) Artillery and ammunition: steady deliveries of 155mm rounds, additional tubes/MLRS and maintenance support to sustain offensive and defensive operations.
4) ISR, EW and air surveillance: timely satellite/AWACS coverage, SIGINT/IMINT sharing and EW capabilities to improve battlespace awareness and force protection.
5) Logistics, engineering and mobility: bridging, heavy lift, fuel, depot and repair support to maintain operational tempo.
6) Personnel and sustainment: UK training teams, maintenance crews and liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed integration and readiness.

Timing: air defence and ammunition resupply are urgent (weeks); building deep‑strike stockpiles and sustainment capacity is critical over the coming months. Please advise what the UK can deliver in the near term and what NATO political/security measures you can mobilize (airspace coordination, basing, accelerated approvals, sanctions alignment). I propose a UK technical delegation meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv within days to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. I can send a prioritized list with quantities immediately. Thank you.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you for that clear, prioritised briefing. We will treat air defence and 155mm ammunition resupply as the immediate UK priorities. In the near term (weeks) the UK can accelerate deliveries of AD munitions and 155mm rounds from available stocks, expedite export and mobilisation approvals, and task logistics and maintenance teams to sustain incoming systems and ammunition. We welcome and accept your proposal for a UK technical delegation to meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. Please send your prioritized list with quantities, preferred systems/interfaces and any lift or basing constraints as soon as possible, and propose available dates for the Kyiv meeting. On the political/security side I will immediately raise coordination with NATO and our partners on airspace deconfliction, basing options and accelerated approvals/sanctions alignment to speed delivery and sustainment. I will prioritise getting a small UK technical team to Kyiv within days once we have your list and dates. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — thank you. Below is Ukraine’s prioritized list (high‑level quantities, preferred systems/interfaces, and lift/basing constraints) for immediate UK technical planning:

1) Air defence (urgent — weeks): 2 long‑range AD batteries (Patriot or equivalent) with initial launcher elements and ~200 interceptors; 6 medium‑range AD systems (NASAMS / IRIS‑T SLM or equivalent) with ~600 interceptors; sustainment spares, IFF/C2 integration (Link‑16 capable), training teams and maintenance detachments. Lift: strategic airlift for systems, routine sealift/road for munitions.

2) 155mm artillery & ammunition (urgent — weeks): total request 200,000 rounds over 3 months, staged deliveries (50k within 4 weeks, 75k within 8 weeks, 75k within 12 weeks). Also request ~100 155mm tubes (mix of towed and SP) and maintenance crews. Lift: sealift + strategic airlift for urgent batches.

3) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires (critical — months): 200–300 precision long‑range munitions (ATACMS/Storm Shadow class or equivalent) with associated targeting assets (UAV designation pods, targeting cell access) and sustainment spares. Requires secure build‑up and secure transport corridors.

4) ISR, EW & air surveillance (high): prioritized satellite tasking, one AWACS rotation commitment, continuous SIGINT/IMINT feeds, and four EW detachments with integration support to fuse into Ukrainian C2.

5) Logistics, engineering & mobility: heavy‑lift / bridging assets, fuel depot stockpiles, forward repair hubs, and UK logistics teams to establish sustainment nodes closer to the front.

6) Personnel & sustainment: deploy 4–6 UK technical/training teams (12–20 personnel each), maintenance crews, and 6–8 liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed system integration and sustainment.

Basing / transport constraints: immediate munitions and spares should flow into allied hubs (Poland/Romania/other) for onward road/rail; long‑range systems need secure airlift and space for integration/testing. We require expedited export approvals, airspace deconfliction for transit, and temporary basing/access where necessary.

Proposed Kyiv meeting: UK technical delegation to Kyiv within 3–5 days. Proposed options: Option A — earliest (in 3 days); Option B — in 5 days. Please confirm your team’s earliest availability and which specialists you will include (AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance). On confirmation I will send a line‑item prioritized list with exact quantities, preferred system variants/interfaces and emplacement/lift requirements for planners.

Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — to finalise the Kyiv meeting please confirm: 1) which option you prefer (Option A — in 3 days; Option B — in 5 days) and your earliest arrival date; 2) team composition (specialists and numbers: AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance, others); and 3) any security, basing or airport/hub support you will require from Ukrainian side. On receipt I will coordinate Ukrainian staff, logistics and provide the detailed line‑item list for planners.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. We confirm Option A: a UK technical delegation will aim to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days (earliest availability). Proposed initial team composition (subject to final adjustment once we receive your line‑item list):

• AD specialists — 6 personnel (systems integration, IFF/Link‑16/C2, operator trainers)
• Munitions & logistics planners — 6 personnel (ammunition planners, strategic/operational lift coordinators)
• C2/EW specialists — 4 personnel (EW integration officers, SIGINT/IMINT liaisons)
• Maintenance detachments — 8 personnel (engineers/technicians for AD and artillery systems)
• Command & liaison — 2 senior officers

Approx. total: ~26 personnel. On support we require from Ukrainian side: secure air corridor/airspace deconfliction to the agreed airfield (Boryspil or alternative), priority handling and customs facilitation for team and urgent equipment, secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection/ground security for personnel and equipment while in Kyiv, and access to allied hubs (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging. Please confirm Option A and the availability of the requested security/basing/hub support and I will issue flight manifests, exact team rosters and equipment lists within 24 hours of your confirmation and on receipt of the detailed line‑item list. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — confirmed. We accept Option A: the UK technical delegation to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days. Ukraine will provide the requested support: airspace deconfliction to the agreed airfield (Boryspil preferred unless you advise otherwise), priority handling and customs facilitation, a secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection/ground security for personnel and equipment while in Kyiv, and access to allied hubs (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging. Ukrainian staff will coordinate reception, secure integration facilities and fast‑track customs and hub movement. Please send flight manifests, the exact team roster and full equipment lists within 24 hours so we can finalise security, ground handling and hub arrangements. Also confirm your preferred airfield and estimated arrival time. Valerii Zaluzhnyi

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. Per your confirmation we are executing Option A: the UK technical delegation will arrive in Kyiv in 3 days. Preferred airfield: Boryspil (please confirm final parking/stand and secure access). Estimated touchdown: in ~72 hours, ETA Boryspil 09:00 local. Below are the flight-manifest summary, exact team roster by role and equipment list for Ukrainian handling, customs and security planning. Please confirm acceptance and advise any restrictions or amendments.

1) Pax roster (total 26):
- Command & liaison: 2 senior officers (lead & deputy)
- Air‑defence specialists: 6 (systems integration lead, IFF/Link‑16/C2 engineer, 2 operator‑trainers, 2 integration technicians)
- Munitions & logistics planners: 6 (ammunition planners, strategic/operational lift coordinators, hub/staging planner)
- C2 / EW specialists: 4 (EW integration officer, SIGINT/IMINT liaison, comms engineer, EW technician)
- Maintenance detachments: 8 (engineers/technicians for AD and 155mm systems: mechanical, electronic, hydraulics, test & calibration)

2) Flight / airlift summary (strategic uplift requested):
- Aircraft: 1x C‑17 (primary heavy lift) + 1x A400M (personnel & light equipment) — slots requested now; if a single heavy lift is preferable we can consolidate onto 2x C‑17. Exact aircraft tail/numbers to follow in formal manifest to UK ACO.
- Pax: 26 plus 6 ground‑crew/aircrew (aircrew will be declared separately).
- Pallet count: up to 12 ULD pallets (heavy integration equipment, spares, containerized technical suites).
- Road/rail onward: containers/pallets to be moved to allied hub (Poland/Romania) or direct to Kyiv secure holding area per your instruction.

3) Equipment list (for priority handling & customs — no live ammunition onboard; munitions staging will use allied hubs):
- AD integration kits: 2 x IFF/Link‑16 gateway boxes, 2 x integration servers, cabling & test harnesses, calibration & radar test gear
- C2 / comms: 4 x secure SATCOM terminals, 6 x encrypted radios, field laptops (hardened) with integration toolchain
- EW / SIGINT test kit: 2 x EW diagnostic racks, 2 portable direction‑finding suites
- Maintenance spares: container of AD & artillery spares (electronic modules, actuators, hydraulic pumps), full tool sets, test meters
- Vehicles & handling: 2 light logistics vehicles (4x4), 1 forklift (air‑portable) or 2 pallet dollies, 1 technical trailer/containerized lab
- Generators & power: 2 x 20 kVA diesel generators + cabling
- Protective & comms: PPE for 26 personnel, standard field protective equipment, medical kit (Role 2 lite)
- Liaison / office: 1 x secure meeting suite (containerized), 1 x printer/scanner, secure comms environment for classified exchanges

4) On‑ground support requested from Ukraine (as you offered):
- Airspace deconfliction and priority handling at Boryspil; confirmed secure corridor to parking stand and priority customs clearance for pax and equipment
- Secure meeting/technical workspace with access control and power hook‑ups for containerized suites
- Close protection and secure movement between airfield and secure facility
- Hub access (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging and onward road/rail coordination

5) Timelines & next steps:
- We will lodge formal aircraft requests and detailed manifests with UK ACO and MOD now. This message contains the final UK delegation roster and equipment list for Ukrainian planning. Formal signed flight manifests with aircraft identifiers, individual names, passport details and exact pallet weights will be sent to you and Ukrainian handling authorities within 24 hours (or sooner if you require); please confirm that Boryspil will accept the listed equipment and provide the requested priority handling and security.

If any element is unacceptable or needs amendment (airfield alternative, constrained pallet count, tighter security requirements), tell us now so we can re‑plan. Once you confirm airfield acceptance and handling slots we will publish the final flight times and manifest to UK and allied logistics nodes. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — received and accepted. Ukraine confirms Boryspil as the preferred airfield and accepts the estimated touchdown of ~09:00 local in ~72 hours. Ukraine will provide the requested parking/stand access, secure corridor, priority handling and customs facilitation, secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection and hub access for munitions staging. The outlined ~26‑person roster and equipment list are accepted (noting no live ammunition onboard; munitions to be staged via allied hubs). Please send the formal signed flight manifests with aircraft tail numbers, individual names and passport details, pallet counts/weights and exact arrival times within 24 hours as you indicated. If aircraft type, arrival time or airfield change, notify immediately so we can reallocate stands and security. We will coordinate final parking/stand assignment, ground handling and protective details on receipt. Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — thank you. While we await the formal manifests, please confirm the NATO/political and security measures you will raise and the timelines so Ukraine can synchronise diplomatic and operational actions: 1) Which specific NATO mechanisms will you activate and when (airspace deconfliction, basing/access for systems, expedited export approvals, sanctions alignment, logistics corridor security)? 2) Who will be our NATO points of contact for operational coordination (AWACS/satellite tasking, SIGINT/IMINT sharing, C2 integration)? 3) Will the UK seek NATO-level approval or political cover for use of allied hubs and temporary basing/access for UK systems, and if so how quickly can that be secured? 4) What force-protection/security support can NATO/UK provide for the delegation, the secure facility in Kyiv and the staging hubs? Ukraine can draft a short briefing for NATO and a proposed list of political actions if that would speed matters — tell us the preferred format and recipient and we will send it immediately. Please advise next steps and expected timelines so we can coordinate on our side.

General Zaluzhnyi — we are now requesting passenger names and passport details from UK MOD/UK ACO and confirming aircraft tail numbers and exact pallet weights with airlift planners. SBU 5‑minute briefing — key points and immediate asks:

- Recent arrests: Vinnytsia resident detained on suspicion of spying for Russia; Kyiv resident arrested for allegedly aiding Russian airstrikes and a separate businessman detained for fencing stolen goods; Kharkiv resident arrested 21 Feb on suspicion of aiding a missile strike. These arrests point to active facilitation networks inside rear areas.

Asks now: authorize synchronized warrants and simultaneous operations; approve temporary enhanced protective measures for air‑defence sites; endorse 30‑day martial‑law extension as requested to enable swift law‑enforcement action. Admiral Radakin — thank you. My immediate operational priorities are:

1) Air defence: integrated medium‑ and long‑range AD systems, interceptors, munitions and sustainment to protect population centers, critical infrastructure and forward units.
2) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires: missiles, guided rockets and targeting support to interdict Russian logistics, command nodes and long‑range launch systems.
3) Artillery and ammunition: steady deliveries of 155mm rounds, additional tubes/MLRS and maintenance support to sustain offensive and defensive operations.
4) ISR, EW and air surveillance: timely satellite/AWACS coverage, SIGINT/IMINT sharing and EW capabilities to improve battlespace awareness and force protection.
5) Logistics, engineering and mobility: bridging, heavy lift, fuel, depot and repair support to maintain operational tempo.
6) Personnel and sustainment: UK training teams, maintenance crews and liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed integration and readiness.

Timing: air defence and ammunition resupply are urgent (weeks); building deep‑strike stockpiles and sustainment capacity is critical over the coming months. Please advise what the UK can deliver in the near term and what NATO political/security measures you can mobilize (airspace coordination, basing, accelerated approvals, sanctions alignment). I propose a UK technical delegation meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv within days to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. I can send a prioritized list with quantities immediately. Thank you.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you for that clear, prioritised briefing. We will treat air defence and 155mm ammunition resupply as the immediate UK priorities. In the near term (weeks) the UK can accelerate deliveries of AD munitions and 155mm rounds from available stocks, expedite export and mobilisation approvals, and task logistics and maintenance teams to sustain incoming systems and ammunition. We welcome and accept your proposal for a UK technical delegation to meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. Please send your prioritized list with quantities, preferred systems/interfaces and any lift or basing constraints as soon as possible, and propose available dates for the Kyiv meeting. On the political/security side I will immediately raise coordination with NATO and our partners on airspace deconfliction, basing options and accelerated approvals/sanctions alignment to speed delivery and sustainment. I will prioritise getting a small UK technical team to Kyiv within days once we have your list and dates. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — thank you. Below is Ukraine’s prioritized list (high‑level quantities, preferred systems/interfaces, and lift/basing constraints) for immediate UK technical planning:

1) Air defence (urgent — weeks): 2 long‑range AD batteries (Patriot or equivalent) with initial launcher elements and ~200 interceptors; 6 medium‑range AD systems (NASAMS / IRIS‑T SLM or equivalent) with ~600 interceptors; sustainment spares, IFF/C2 integration (Link‑16 capable), training teams and maintenance detachments. Lift: strategic airlift for systems, routine sealift/road for munitions.

2) 155mm artillery & ammunition (urgent — weeks): total request 200,000 rounds over 3 months, staged deliveries (50k within 4 weeks, 75k within 8 weeks, 75k within 12 weeks). Also request ~100 155mm tubes (mix of towed and SP) and maintenance crews. Lift: sealift + strategic airlift for urgent batches.

3) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires (critical — months): 200–300 precision long‑range munitions (ATACMS/Storm Shadow class or equivalent) with associated targeting assets (UAV designation pods, targeting cell access) and sustainment spares. Requires secure build‑up and secure transport corridors.

4) ISR, EW & air surveillance (high): prioritized satellite tasking, one AWACS rotation commitment, continuous SIGINT/IMINT feeds, and four EW detachments with integration support to fuse into Ukrainian C2.

5) Logistics, engineering & mobility: heavy‑lift / bridging assets, fuel depot stockpiles, forward repair hubs, and UK logistics teams to establish sustainment nodes closer to the front.

6) Personnel & sustainment: deploy 4–6 UK technical/training teams (12–20 personnel each), maintenance crews, and 6–8 liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed system integration and sustainment.

Basing / transport constraints: immediate munitions and spares should flow into allied hubs (Poland/Romania/other) for onward road/rail; long‑range systems need secure airlift and space for integration/testing. We require expedited export approvals, airspace deconfliction for transit, and temporary basing/access where necessary.

Proposed Kyiv meeting: UK technical delegation to Kyiv within 3–5 days. Proposed options: Option A — earliest (in 3 days); Option B — in 5 days. Please confirm your team’s earliest availability and which specialists you will include (AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance). On confirmation I will send a line‑item prioritized list with exact quantities, preferred system variants/interfaces and emplacement/lift requirements for planners.

Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — to finalise the Kyiv meeting please confirm: 1) which option you prefer (Option A — in 3 days; Option B — in 5 days) and your earliest arrival date; 2) team composition (specialists and numbers: AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance, others); and 3) any security, basing or airport/hub support you will require from Ukrainian side. On receipt I will coordinate Ukrainian staff, logistics and provide the detailed line‑item list for planners.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. We confirm Option A: a UK technical delegation will aim to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days (earliest availability). Proposed initial team composition (subject to final adjustment once we receive your line‑item list):

• AD specialists — 6 personnel (systems integration, IFF/Link‑16/C2, operator trainers)

Once you confirm airfield acceptance and handling slots we will publish the final flight times and manifest to UK and allied logistics nodes. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — received and accepted. Ukraine confirms Boryspil as the preferred airfield and accepts the estimated touchdown of ~09:00 local in ~72 hours. Ukraine will provide the requested parking/stand access, secure corridor, priority handling and customs facilitation, secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection and hub access for munitions staging. The outlined ~26‑person roster and equipment list are accepted (noting no live ammunition onboard; munitions to be staged via allied hubs). Please send the formal signed flight manifests with aircraft tail numbers, individual names and passport details, pallet counts/weights and exact arrival times within 24 hours as you indicated. If aircraft type, arrival time or airfield change, notify immediately so we can reallocate stands and security. We will coordinate final parking/stand assignment, ground handling and protective details on receipt. Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — thank you. While we await the formal manifests, please confirm the NATO/political and security measures you will raise and the timelines so Ukraine can synchronise diplomatic and operational actions: 1) Which specific NATO mechanisms will you activate and when (airspace deconfliction, basing/access for systems, expedited export approvals, sanctions alignment, logistics corridor security)? 2) Who will be our NATO points of contact for operational coordination (AWACS/satellite tasking, SIGINT/IMINT sharing, C2 integration)? 3) Will the UK seek NATO-level approval or political cover for use of allied hubs and temporary basing/access for UK systems, and if so how quickly can that be secured? 4) What force-protection/security support can NATO/UK provide for the delegation, the secure facility in Kyiv and the staging hubs? Ukraine can draft a short briefing for NATO and a proposed list of political actions if that would speed matters — tell us the preferred format and recipient and we will send it immediately. Please advise next steps and expected timelines so we can coordinate on our side.

General Zaluzhnyi — we are now requesting passenger names and passport details from UK MOD/UK ACO and confirming aircraft tail numbers and exact pallet weights with airlift planners. We will compile and send formal signed flight manifests (aircraft tail numbers, individual names and passport details, pallet counts/weights and exact arrival times) to you and UK ACO within 24 hours. Please confirm whether you require aircrew declared on the manifest and whether the nominated parking/stand at Boryspil requires any additional advance liaison for ground handling. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Presenting now: confirmed overnight strikes across Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts. Confirmed casualties so far: two injured (one in Zaporizhzhia city, one in Kryvyi Rih). Damage assessments ongoing. Immediate recommendations for presidential/operational approval: 1) Raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD assets to high‑risk southern sectors; 2) SBU & GUR: launch joint forensic debris recovery and origin analysis immediately, nominate liaisons to MoD; 3) MoD/Syrskyi: prepare interdiction and counter‑strike options pending validated launch site attribution and lawful clearance; 4) Police & regional civil‑defense: activate shelters, secure critical infrastructure, preposition emergency medical and humanitarian response teams to affected oblasts; 5) Communications: issue a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports; 6) Request partner ISR and AD data (NATO/Bilateral) to accelerate attribution and tracking. I request permission to implement items 1–5 now and to circulate full damage reports and targetable intelligence within the hour.

Requesting presidential authorization to implement recommended measures now: 1) Raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD assets to high‑risk southern sectors; 2) SBU & GUR to begin joint forensic debris recovery and origin analysis and nominate liaisons to MoD; 3) MoD/Syrskyi to prepare interdiction and counter‑strike options pending validated attribution and lawful clearance; 4) Police & regional civil‑defense to activate shelters, secure critical infrastructure, and preposition medical/humanitarian teams; 5) Communications: issue a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports. President Zelenskyy — do I have your authorization to implement items 1–5 immediately? Syrskyi/Oleshchuk/Budanov/SBU/GUR — confirm capability and ETA to execute.

Mr President — while frontline reports proceed per your instruction, I request your explicit authorization to implement the recommended measures now. Specifically: 1) raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD assets to high‑risk southern sectors (to be reversible on your order); 2) SBU & GUR to begin joint forensic debris recovery and nominate liaisons to MoD immediately; 3) MoD to prepare interdiction and counter‑strike options pending validated attribution and lawful clearance; 4) police & regional civil‑defense to activate shelters, secure critical infrastructure, and preposition medical/humanitarian teams to affected oblasts; 5) communications: issue a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports. I request approval to begin items 1 and 4 immediately and to circulate full damage reports and targetable intelligence within the hour. Syrskyi / Oleshchuk / Budanov / SBU / GUR — confirm capability and ETA to execute. President Zelenskyy — do I have your authorization to proceed with items 1–5 (or at least 1 and 4 now)?

Mr President — frontline reports are underway. I request your explicit authorization to implement the recommended measures now: 1) raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD assets to high‑risk southern sectors; 2) SBU & GUR to begin joint forensic debris recovery and nominate liaisons to MoD; 3) MoD to prepare interdiction/counter‑strike options pending validated attribution and lawful clearance; 4) police & regional civil‑defense to activate shelters, secure critical infrastructure, and preposition medical/humanitarian teams; 5) communications: issue a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports. May I proceed immediately with items 1 and 4 and with items 2–5 as described? Please confirm.

Mr President — GUR has granted permission to implement items 1–5. SBU & GUR are ready to begin joint forensic debris recovery and nominate liaisons; MoD/Syrskyi have prepared interdiction/counter‑strike options pending attribution and legal clearance; police & regional civil‑defense are prepared to activate shelters and preposition medical teams. May I have your explicit authorization to begin implementation now — to raise AD posture and activate shelters immediately (items 1 and 4) and to proceed with items 2–5 as described?

Mr President — I request your explicit authorization to begin implementation now: 1) raise AD posture and reallocate mobile AD to high‑risk southern sectors; 4) activate shelters and preposition medical and humanitarian teams. Do you approve starting items 1 and 4 immediately? Do you also authorize items 2–5 (joint forensic recovery and liaison, MoD targeting prep pending attribution/legal clearance, police/civil‑defense measures, and a short public advisory) to proceed as described? Please confirm.

Authorized. I authorize immediate implementation of items 1 and 4 now: (1) raise nationwide air‑defence posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD assets to high‑risk southern sectors; (4) activate shelters and preposition emergency medical and humanitarian response teams to affected oblasts. I also authorize SBU & GUR to begin joint forensic debris recovery and to nominate liaisons to MoD (item 2), and MoD to prepare interdiction/counter‑strike options pending validated attribution (item 3). Podolyak/Yermak — draft a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports; hold for rapid clearance. Government/Mod — prioritise transport corridors and military police escorts for redeployment. Syrskyi / Oleshchuk / Budanov / SBU / GUR / Police — confirm capability and ETA to execute items 1 and 4 now. Oleshchuk — begin re‑tasking mobile SAM batteries and provide a redeployment timeline and expected coverage within 45 minutes. Budanov — deliver initial intelligence/attribution packet within 45–60 minutes. Report confirmations immediately.

Immediate confirmations required now: 

1) Mykola Oleshchuk — confirm you will deliver the parts & munitions priority list in 30 minutes, the phased redeployment timeline (unit-by-unit movements and expected coverage) in 45 minutes, and nominate an Air Force HQ liaison to the joint C2 cell within 10 minutes. Confirm you will begin re-tasking on approval. 

2) Oleksandr Syrskyi / Ministry of Defence — confirm allocation/dispatch of two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) and priority rail/road corridors and military police escorts for immediate movement of Reserve Battery Alpha & Bravo. Confirm MOD readiness to release prioritized AD munitions/fuel per Oleshchuk’s upcoming list. 

3) SBU (Ihor Klymenko) / GUR (Budanov) — confirm nomination of a single validated-target liaison to the Air Force, assignment of SBU protective detachments for battery movement and depot security, and commitment to joint forensic debris recovery. Budanov — confirm delivery of initial intelligence/attribution packet within 45–60 minutes. 

4) Podolyak / Yermak / Government — prepare a short public advisory (shelter guidance, caution vs unverified reports) for rapid clearance. 

Report single-line confirmations and ETAs immediately.

Proposed public advisory for rapid clearance: Overnight drone strikes affected southern oblasts. For the public: 1) Seek shelter immediately when air‑raid warnings sound and remain until the all‑clear; 2) Follow instructions from local authorities and official government channels only; 3) Do not repost or act on unverified reports — await official confirmation; 4) If safe, report emergencies to local emergency services and follow shelter/humanitarian instructions. Please review and approve for immediate release. — Mykhailo Podolyak

Draft advisory for rapid clearance: Overnight drone strikes affected southern oblasts. For the public: 1) Seek shelter immediately when air‑raid warnings sound and remain until the all‑clear; 2) Follow instructions from local authorities and official government channels only; 3) Do not repost or act on unverified reports — await official confirmation; 4) If safe, report emergencies to local emergency services and follow shelter/humanitarian instructions. Please clear for immediate release. — Mykhailo Podolyak

Генерал Аксенов — срочный доклад по состоянию и принимаемым мерам.

1) Взрывы в Севастополе: проверка и ликвидация последствий ведутся. Подтверждённых сводных данных по массовым жертвам на данный момент нет — сведения уточняются оперативно. Экстренные службы и ПВО приведены в повышенную готовность. Идёт первичное обследование объектов хранения топлива и складов; детальная сводка о повреждениях и рисках горения/утечек будет направлена в течение 4 часов.

2) Обстановка в Чёрном море и блокада: контроль за прибрежной зоной и блокада поддерживаются; патрулирование, разведка и ЭВР выполняются по имеющимся задачам, частота угроз и активность БПЛА/ударов остаются повышенными.

3) Состояние флагмана «МОСКВА»: временно в ближней припортовой стоянке (точные причалы — у мэра/портслужб). Ходовая/двигательная часть частично работоспособна; корпус и ходовая часть получили повреждения средней—тяжёлой степени; требуется ввод в док и возможная буксировка в крупный сухой док. Оценочные сроки работ при текущей неопределённости доковой доступности: оптимистично ~7 дн / типично ~21 дн / пессимистично до ~60 дн. Требуется тяжёлая подъёмно-буксировочная и доковая поддержка, специализированные ремонтные бригады и ключевые запчасти (двигатели/валы/редукторы, радиолокация и коммуникации).

4) Порт, тыл, запасы: грузовые и ремонтные мощности порта ограничены; в порту отмечено ~2 буксира (требуется проверка силы буксировки); тяжёлые плавкраны/подъёмники и специализированные судоремонтные бригады — в дефиците. Боезапас и топливо под давлением — оценки уточняются, приоритет — срочное пополнение критических видов боеприпасов и судового топлива.

5) ПВО / ЭВ / РОБ / противодействие БПЛА: береговые среднего́/ближнего радиуса установлены в отдельных секторах; наблюдается дефицит систем дальнего радиуса (S‑400) и достаточного количества ближней ПВО (Pantsir/CIWS), а также модулей EW и средств противодействия БПЛА. ПВО поставлено в режим повышенной готовности; усиление необходимо срочно.

6) Срочные приоритеты (прошу немедленной координации с центром в порядке приоритета):
  • Немедленно выделить/перенаправить крупный сухой док или тяжёлый плавдок и тяжёлые буксиры; организовать перегруз и буксировку «МОСКВЫ» при подтверждённых условиях причаливания.
  • Экстренно подвести комплекты ПВО / EW / средства РЭБ и приоритетно доставить боеприпасы и топливо для поддержания боеготовности порта и кораблей.
  • Увеличить силы траления и охранного эскорта (МИНОЧИСТКА + конвоирование) и направить специализированные ремонтные команды для обеспечения краткосрочной работоспособности причалов и судов.

- Андрeй Короляев, начальник порта — канал Sev-Port-Op

Действия от флота: немедленно формирую запросы в центр по трём приоритетам выше, инициирую вызов ремонтных групп и траления, готовлю расширенную сводку по взрывам и запасам в течение ~4 часов. Прошу подтверждения приоритета на выделение внешних доковых мощностей и разрешение на привлечение внешних ремонтных бригад.

Конец доклада.

Mykola Oleshchuk — please confirm you will send the parts/munitions priority list to the command centre and Podolyak within 30 minutes and the phased redeployment timeline within 45 minutes as stated, and begin re‑tasking on verbal approval. Request SBU, MoD, Air Defence (Oleshchuk) and regional leads to give 2‑minute situational inputs and nominate liaisons to coordinate implementation.

GUR (HUR) confirms capability and will act now. We will commence joint forensic debris recovery and origin analysis immediately and nominate a GUR liaison to MoD and SBU for direct coordination. Provide ETA to deploy field recovery teams to prioritized sites (Dnipro/Kryvyi Rih/Mykolaiv/Zaporizhzhia) and confirm you can deliver a preliminary forensic/targetable intelligence package within 60 minutes. Do you require additional presidential/legal go/no‑go beyond the room’s authorizations to circulate targetable intel to MoD/GUR and select partners? data.content: Увага — термінова координаційна нарада. Всі присутні (Budanov, GUR, Klitschko, Klymenko, Kyrylenko, Oleshchuk, Podolyak, SBU, Syrskyi, Government, Yermak, Zelenskyy) збираються у головній залі координації оборони в Києві за 10 хвилин (можна почати негайно). Порядок дня: 1) актуальна розвідка та загрози (GUR, SBU); 2) оперативна ситуація на фронті і негайні бойові накази (Syrskyi, Budanov); 3) правопорядок та цивільний захист (Klymenko, Klitschko, Kyrylenko); 4) ПВО, логістика, урядові рішення та координація зовнішньої політики (Oleshchuk, Podolyak, Yermak, Government, Zelenskyy). Принести оновлені карти, розвіддані та пропозиції оперативних рішень. Засідання веде Президент. Якщо хтось не може прибути — доповідач має надати тезисну довідку зараз.

Коротко — SITREP від Podolyak: нічні удари БПЛА по Дніпропетровській, Миколаївській, Запорізькій і Херсонській областях; наразі підтверджено 2 поранених (Запоріжжя, Кривий Ріг); оцінки пошкоджень і походження уламків у роботі.

Негайні маршрутизація/накази (виконувати зараз, підтвердити ETA 10–15 хв):
1) Mykhailo Podolyak — розіслати повні звіти про пошкодження і цільову розвідку в цей зал, регіональним координаторам, Andriy Yermak і Government of Ukraine протягом 60 хв (можна починати зараз після підтвердження). 
2) Andriy Yermak / Government — підготувати коротке узгоджене зовнішнє повідомлення та оперативні запити партнерам (Brussels/Washington); погодити фіналізований текст у залі. 
3) Pavlo Kyrylenko — забезпечити надходження секторних SITREP (Київ, Північ, Схід, Південь, Захід) у цей зал протягом 10–15 хв. 
4) Mykola Oleshchuk — підвищити постур ППО і почати тимчасове перерозподілення мобільних засобів на південь; вкажіть ETA на перекидання. 
5) Oleksandr Syrskyi / MoD — підготуйте варіанти перехоплення/контрзаходів (юридична оцінка), вкажіть ETA на готовність. 
6) Kyrylo Budanov / SBU / GUR — почати судово‑технічне вилучення уламків і аналіз походження, призначити ліаїзонів до MoD; підтвердьте можливість та ETA. 
7) Police / Klymenko / Klitschko — активувати укриття, захист КІ та розгорнути медичні/гуманітарні резерви; підтвердьте ETA.

Підтвердіть виконання та ETA на першочергові заходи (10–15 хв). Podolyak — після підтвердження надсилайте повні матеріали в зал і регіони; можна виконувати пункти 1 і 4 зараз.

Коротко — підсумок від Podolyak: нічні удари БПЛА по Дніпропетровській, Миколаївській, Запорізькій і Херсонській областях; підтверджено 2 поранених (Запоріжжя, Кривий Ріг); оцінки пошкоджень та походження уламків у роботі.

Президент авторизував негайну реалізацію пунктів 1 і 4 (підвищення постур ППО та тимчасове перерозподілення мобільних ППО на південь; активація укриттів і розгортання мед/гуманітарних команд). Інші пункти тримати в режимі готовності.

Негайні маршрутизація/накази (підтвердити можливість і ETA в 10–15 хв):
- Mykhailo Podolyak: розіслати повні звіти про пошкодження й цільову розвідку в цей зал, регіональним координаторам, Andriy Yermak і Government of Ukraine протягом 60 хв — надсилайте після підтверджень.
- Andriy Yermak / Government: підготувати єдине коротке зовнішнє повідомлення і оперативні запити партнерам (Brussels/Washington); винести фінальний текст у залі для погодження (ETA 30–60 хв).
- Pavlo Kyrylenko: зібрати секторні SITREP (Київ, Північ, Схід, Південь, Захід) і надати до цієї зали протягом 10–15 хв.
- Mykola Oleshchuk: підвищити постур ППО і почати тимчасове перерозподілення мобільних засобів на південь; вкажіть ETA на перекидання.
- Oleksandr Syrskyi / MoD: підготувати варіанти перехоплення/контрзаходів з юридичною оцінкою; вкажіть ETA на готовність.
- Kyrylo Budanov / GUR / SBU: почати судово‑технічне вилучення уламків і аналіз походження, призначити ліаїзонів до MoD; підтвердьте можливість та ETA.
- Ihor Klymenko / Police / Vitali Klitschko: активувати укриття, захистити критичну інфраструктуру, розгорнути медичні і гуманітарні резерви; підтвердьте ETA.

Усім: підтвердьте можливість виконання і надайте ETA на першочергові заходи (10–15 хв). Podolyak — після підтвердження розсилайте повні матеріали в зал, регіони і Yermak/Government; пункти 1 і 4 можна виконувати зараз.

Підсумок SITREP (Podolyak): нічні удари БПЛА по Дніпропетровській, Миколаївській, Запорізькій і Херсонській областях; підтверджено 2 поранених (Запоріжжя, Кривий Ріг); оцінки пошкоджень та походження уламків — у роботі.

Негайні накази — виконувати зараз, підтвердити ETA 10–15 хв:
1) Mykhailo Podolyak — розіслати повні звіти про пошкодження та цільову розвідку до цього залу, регіональних координаторів, Andriy Yermak та Government of Ukraine протягом 60 хв (можна починати зараз після підтверджень).
2) Andriy Yermak / Government — підготувати узгоджене коротке зовнішнє повідомлення (інструкції щодо укриттів, уникати неперевірених повідомлень) і оперативні запити до партнерів (Brussels/Washington); представити фінальний текст у залі (ETA 30–60 хв).
3) Pavlo Kyrylenko — зібрати секторні SITREP (Київ, Північ, Схід, Південь, Захід) і надати їх у цей зал протягом 10–15 хв.
4) Mykola Oleshchuk — підвищити постур ППО і почати тимчасове переміщення мобільних засобів в південні сектори; вкажіть ETA на перекидання.
5) Oleksandr Syrskyi / MoD — підготуйте варіанти перехоплення/контрзаходів з юридичною оцінкою; вкажіть ETA на готовність.
6) Kyrylo Budanov / GUR / SBU — почати судово‑технічне вилучення уламків і аналіз походження, призначити ліаїзонів до MoD; підтвердьте можливість і ETA.
7) Ihor Klymenko / Police / Vitali Klitschko — активувати укриття, захистити критичну інфраструктуру, розгорнути медичні/гуманітарні резерви; підтвердьте ETA.

Президент авторизував негайне виконання пунктів 1 і 4 (підвищення постур ППО та тимчасове перерозподілення мобільних ППО на південь; активація укриттів і розгортання мед/гуманітарних команд). Інші пункти — тримати в режимі готовності.

Підтвердіть виконання і надайте ETA на першочергові заходи (10–15 хв). Podolyak — після підтвердження надсилайте повні матеріали в цей зал і регіони.

Mr President, colleagues — Donetsk Oblast 5‑minute situational & civil‑defense brief (summary and immediate asks):

1) Frontline situation: active heavy fighting continues along the frontline sectors facing Donetsk city and Avdiivka‑Pokrovsk axis; frontlines are fluid with targeted enemy strikes on rear‑area infrastructure. Sector commanders report localized tactical withdrawals to prepared positions where forced; further details to follow in written SITREP.

2) Civilian casualties & damage: preliminary reports indicate civilian casualties and multiple damaged residential and utility sites; full casualty and damage tallies are still being collected—estimates will be provided within 60 minutes once local administrations and emergency services consolidate their reports.

3) Shelter & evacuation capacity: current state shelters in government‑controlled parts of the oblast are stressed; existing shelter stocks (bedding, generators, potable water) are insufficient for a larger displacement wave. Request immediate prepositioning of additional shelter kits, mobile generators, and potable‑water tanking. Request Klitschko/Government to confirm extra shelter space and short‑term housing options.

4) Critical infrastructure status: intermittent power and water outages reported in several settlements; communications degraded in contested areas. Immediate priority: restore localized power to hospitals and water pumping stations; preposition mobile power units and fuel to keep lifesaving services running.

5) Immediate humanitarian requests (hours): deploy trauma/forward surgical teams (minimum 2–3 mobile surgical/trauma teams), emergency medical kits (blood, tranexamic acid, trauma packs), ambulances and fuel, emergency food and water parcels for displaced families, shelter kits (tents, blankets, generators), and psychosocial support teams. Request international assistance channels be activated for specialized trauma consumables and mobile hospital modules.

6) Engineering & demining needs: urgent engineering support to clear/verify evacuation routes and to stabilize damaged bridges/roads. Request rapid‑response demining teams and heavy engineering equipment (excavators, graders) to be prioritized for Donetsk to enable humanitarian access and evacuations.

7) Logistics & movement: request prioritized fuel allocations, secure transport corridors and military police/escort for humanitarian convoys. Need immediate convoy escorts for fuel, medical supplies, and shelter materiel; request designated safe‑corridor windows and MLRS/long‑range fires deconfliction for routes in use.

8) Urgent security & SBU asks: protective detachments for air‑defence units and recovery teams; SBU to continue protective cordons at recovery sites and nominate liaison to regional admin for evidence collection and CI screening of contractors/suppliers.

9) Military support requests (urgent): air‑defence coverage over populated centres and key logistics nodes in Donetsk Oblast; temporary redeployment of mobile AD assets (or allocation of available interceptors) to cover major urban areas and critical infrastructure approach routes; protective escorts for AD re‑deployment convoys; estimate ETAs requested from MoD/Oleshchuk/Syrskyi for when AD coverage can be provided or augmented for Donetsk (ideally within 30–45 minutes for initial redeployment timeline, detailed unit‑by‑unit within 45 minutes).

Immediate asks and actions requested now:
- MoD/Syrskyi/Oleshchuk: confirm capability and ETA to provide/augment AD coverage for Donetsk and protective detachments for AD units; provide redeployment timeline within 45 minutes. 
- SBU: nominate protective detachments and a liaison to regional admin; confirm ability to secure recovery teams and cordons within 2–6 hours. 
- Government/Podolyak/Klitschko: authorize and arrange immediate prepositioning of trauma teams, shelter kits, mobile generators, water, and food; designate assembly points and coordinate transport escorts. 
- Engineering/DEM: allocate demining and heavy engineering assets to clear evacuation routes; confirm ETA for first teams.

data.content: Mr. President, Ministers, Colleagues — I will give a short briefing on Moscow's security and civil‑defence readiness and request immediate coordination of municipal measures. Current posture: Moscow city services are on high alert and standing by; emergency crews, medical teams and municipal utilities are being prepared for rapid deployment; shelter and medical capacity is being readied city‑wide. I request your immediate authorization to: (a) coordinate air/ground security and situation awareness with the General Staff and Ministry of Defence; (b) activate civil‑defence measures, open designated shelters, and implement targeted transport restrictions where required; (c) mobilize municipal emergency teams and priority crews for power, water and communications resilience; (d) release clear public instructions via the Kremlin press office and faith/community channels to prevent panic. I ask for guidance and authorization to execute these measures now.

Господа, благодарю за немедленную авторизацию. В подтверждение и для дальнейшей координации направляю сводку муниципальных ресурсов и вопросы, требующие подтверждения: 

1) Перечень и вместимость обозначенных укрытий (оперативный свод): 
- Метрополитен (выделено станции глубокого заложения) — ориентировочная общая вместимость ~600 000 человек; 
- 25 капитальных подземных убежищ ГО в центральных округах — суммарно ~60 000 человек; 
- Крытые спортивные комплексы/подвальные резервные площади — резерв ~40 000 человек. 
Полный подробный список с адресами и координатами готов выслать в этом канале в течение 10 минут. 

2) Медицинские мощности: городской резерв интенсивной помощи — ~2 500 коек (включая ~300 аппаратов ИВЛ); 40 мобильных реанимационных бригад; 6 полевых госпиталей готовы к развёртыванию. Подробный список стационаров, текущая загрузка и контакты — отправлю по защищённому каналу/в этом канале по указанию. 

3) Контакты экстренных служб (дежурные): Оперативный штаб Мэра (дежурный), Координационный центр медицины катастроф, Центр управления городским хозяйством — пришлю расширённый контакт‑лист с резервными номерами и радиоканалами для оперативной связи. 

4) Процедуры медэвакуации и сопровождения колонн: предлагаемая процедура — маршруты эвакуации и коридоры согласуются городским штабом с Генштабом; колонны скорой/реанимации получают оперативное разрешение и, при необходимости, сопровождение/эскорт со стороны сил безопасности; при непосредственной угрозе Минобороны обеспечивает прикрытие и сопровождение по согласованным координатам. Прошу подтвердить, что это соответствует процедурам Минобороны/Генштаба, и прислать регламент сопровождения колонн (порядок запроса сопровождения, сроки реакции, ответственные каналы). 

5) Обмен данными ПВО: прошу установить постоянный защищённый канал обмена целевой ситуационной информацией (реальное время) между дежурными пунктами Минобороны/Генштаба и городской ситуационной группой; прошу указать технические параметры/учётные данные канала и ответственных лиц для непрерывной синхронизации. 

6) Публичные инструкции: согласен, что тексты следует согласовать с пресс‑службой Кремля; прошу указать — разрешаете ли вы сейчас выпускать оперативные инструкции через пресс‑службу Кремля и религиозные/муниципальные каналы (ответ «да»/«нет»). 

Прошу письменного подтверждения/ответа по пунктам 4–6 и формальной (скан/ответ в этом канале) авторизации на: A) активацию муниципальных убежищ; B) введение целевых транспортных ограничений; C) мобилизацию приоритетных аварийных бригад (энергетика, вода, связь, медицина); D) установление защищённого канала обмена с Минобороны/Генштабом. 

Немедленно после получения письменного подтверждения вышлю полные списки убежищ, медицинских мощностей и расширенный контакт‑лист для подписи/утверждения.

Срочно — в конференц-зал Кремля. Прошу немедленного присутствия всех для брифинга по срыву переговоров в Анталье, последствиям для соглашения о вывозе зерна из Чёрного моря и предлагаемым мерам реагирования.
Всем присутствующим — немедленно в конференц-зал Кремля. Начинаю брифинг по срыву переговоров в Анталье, последствиям для соглашения о вывозе зерна из Чёрного моря и предлагаемым мерам реагирования.

Принято. Немедленно направляюсь в конференц‑зал Кремля и прошу всех присутствующих присоединиться. Москва готовит краткий оперативный доклад по вопросам безопасности, гражданской обороны и готовности инфраструктуры в связи со срывом переговоров и возможными последствиями для экспорта зерна; прошу прислать повестку и любые материалы/оценки угроз, которые следует включить. Готов выступить сразу после начала.

Господа, благодарю за письменную авторизацию. Подтверждаю получение и докладываю о дальнейших шагах: 

1) Москва немедленно приступает к активации муниципальных убежищ, введению целевых транспортных ограничений и мобилизации приоритетных аварийных бригад (энергетика, вода, связь, медицина). 

2) В течение 10 минут по защищённому каналу вышлю и одновременно пришлю копию в этот канал: а) полный список убежищ с адресами и координатами; б) детализованные данные по стационарам (текущая загрузка, число коек интенсивной помощи, аппаратов ИВЛ, контактные лица); в) расширенный контакт‑лист аварийных служб с резервными номерами и радиоканалами.

3) Прошу прислать по защищённому каналу/в этом канале: A) технические параметры защищённого канала (тип шифрования, адреса/учётные записи, контакт оператора/ответственного лица); B) официальный регламент медэвакуации и сопровождения колонн (форма запроса, максимальные сроки реакции, ответственные контакты, порядок подтверждения эскорта); C) формат и параметры передачи данных ПВО (координаты/сетка vs. адреса, приоритет сообщений) и контакт дежурного для прямой синхронизации. 

4) Доложим о ходе выполнения по каждому основному пункту в течение 30 минут и немедленно отправим через защищённый канал любые критические потребности. 

С уважением, Сергей Собянин, Мэр Москвы

Принято. Подготовил план действий и краткую сводку готовности для сегодняшнего совещания. В план включены: 1) мероприятия по обеспечению безопасности верующих и храмов (маршруты прибытия, организация охраны, необходимые укрытия); 2) порядок активации муниципальных убежищ и их развёртывания; 3) целевые транспортные ограничения и коридоры для медэвакуации; 4) мобилизация аварийных бригад (энергетика, вода, связь) и медицинских резервов; 5) организация защищённого обмена ПВО‑данными и оперативная синхронизация с Минобороны/Генштабом. Готов выступить немедленно в конференц‑зале и представить письменную версию плана. Прошу Минобороны/Генштаб предоставить подписанные оперативные рекомендации и оценки угроз для стола Президента и представить их устно/письменно в зале; прошу пресс‑службу Кремля подготовить согласованный текст оперативных инструкций для немедленного выпуска. С уважением, Сергей Собянин.

Министерство обороны и Генштаб — представить в конференц‑зале 5‑минутную устную сводку по пунктам, указанным в распоряжении Кремля: 1) ключевые выводы по оперативной обстановке; 2) поэтапный план немедленной мобилизации (сроки, ответственные, ресурсы); 3) правовые и организационно‑практические варианты интеграции/аннексии и риски; 4) оперативные предложения по обеспечению безопасности морских коридоров и вывоза зерна; 5) первоочередные потребности для координации с московскими службами по гражданской защите. Прошу также немедленно передать подписанные письменные рекомендации на стол Президента. Собянин — обеспечить меры безопасности для гражданских объектов и культовых сооружений. Песков — подготовить и принести проект заявления для зачтения сразу после брифинга.

Песков, зачитайте, пожалуйста, проект пресс‑заявления сейчас. Прошу по очереди краткие замечания: Минобороны/Генштаб — до 2 минут (оперативные корректировки и подписи); мэр Собянин — готовность по гражданской защите; пресс‑служба — корректность формулировок; остальные — только существенные правки. После замечаний прошу зачитать обновлённый текст для окончательного согласования и подписей.

message.content:
Генерал Аксенов — срочный доклад по состоянию и принимаемым мерам.

1) Взрывы в Севастополе: проверка и ликвидация последствий ведутся. Подтверждённых сводных данных по массовым жертвам на данный момент нет — сведения уточняются оперативно. Экстренные службы и ПВО приведены в повышенную готовность. Идёт первичное обследование объектов хранения топлива и складов; детальная сводка о повреждениях и рисках горения/утечек будет направлена в течение 4 часов.

2) Обстановка в Чёрном море и блокада: контроль за прибрежной зоной и блокада поддерживаются; патрулирование, разведка и ЭВР выполняются по имеющимся задачам, частота угроз и активность БПЛА/ударов остаются повышенными.

3) Состояние флагмана «МОСКВА»: временно в ближней припортовой стоянке (точные причалы — у мэра/портслужб). Ходовая/двигательная часть частично работоспособна; корпус и ходовая часть получили повреждения средней—тяжёлой степени; требуется ввод в док и возможная буксировка в крупный сухой док. Оценочные сроки работ при текущей неопределённости доковой доступности: оптимистично ~7 дн / типично ~21 дн / пессимистично до ~60 дн. Требуется тяжёлая подъёмно-буксировочная и доковая поддержка, специализированные ремонтные бригады и ключевые запчасти (двигатели/валы/редукторы, радиолокация и коммуникации).

4) Порт, тыл, запасы: грузовые и ремонтные мощности порта ограничены; в порту отмечено ~2 буксира (требуется проверка силы буксировки); тяжёлые плавкраны/подъёмники и специализированные судоремонтные бригады — в дефиците. Боезапас и топливо под давлением — оценки уточняются, приоритет — срочное пополнение критических видов боеприпасов и судового топлива.

params.text: 在塞瓦斯托波尔，官员Aksyonov向黑海舰队报告：市内发生爆炸事件，正在核查与处置；目前无确认大规模伤亡，紧急救援和防空力量已提升至高度戒备；对燃料/仓储设施的初步检查正在进行，详细损毁与火险/泄漏评估将在约4小时内提交。Aksyonov列出对舰队/港口的三项紧急需求并请求立刻向中央协调：1) 立即调配大型干船坞或重型浮船坞及重型拖轮，组织对“莫斯科号”的转运/入坞；2) 紧急增拨防空（远/中/近程）、电子战與反无人设备，并优先补给弹药与燃油；3) 增派扫雷与护航编队并派遣专业修理队伍保障码头与航道短期可用性。Aksyonov报告本港约有2艘拖轮、浮/干坞容量有限、重型吊装与舰级检修队与关键备件短缺、弹药与燃油库存承压。Aksyonov抄送并确认的现场联络人：港务处长 安德烈·科罗廖夫 (Sev-Port-Op)；港务局副局长 伊琳娜·马卡洛娃 (Sev-Log-2)；造船厂主管 维克托·列维琴科 (Sev-Shipyard)；后勤处长 娜塔莉娅·苏霍娃 (Sev-Log-1)；防空指挥官 尤里·斯米尔诺夫 (Sev-AAD)；扫雷负责人 叶夫根尼·彼得罗夫 (Sev-MCM)。

data.text: 在塞瓦斯托波尔，官员阿克肖诺夫向黑海舰队报告市内发生爆炸事件，正在核查与处置。
阿克肖诺夫报告目前尚无确认大规模伤亡，紧急救援与防空力量已提升至高度戒备。

阿克肖诺夫表示详细损毁及火险/泄漏评估将在约4小时内提交。
阿克肖诺夫请求立即调配大型干船坞或重型浮船坞及重型拖轮，以组织对“莫斯科号”的转运与入坞，并请求中央立刻协调。
阿克肖诺夫请求紧急增拨防空（远/中/近程）、电子战与反无人机设备，并优先补给弹药与燃油，已请求中央立刻协调。
阿克肖诺夫请求增派扫雷与护航编队并派遣专业修理队伍，以保障码头与航道的短期可用性，并请求中央立刻协调。

SBU response to Podolyak (for the room): Confirming capability and immediate actions.

1) Forensic recovery & origin analysis (Podolyak item 2): SBU will launch joint forensic debris‑recovery teams with GUR immediately. Teams and equipment are being readied now; we can task and nominate SBU liaisons to MoD within 30 minutes. Field recovery teams can deploy to prioritized sites (Dnipro/Kherson/Mykolaiv/Zaporizhzhia) within ~2 hours, subject to MoD clearance for ISZ entry; request Syrskyi confirm safe‑work windows and escort availability.

2) Intelligence product & circulation: SBU can prepare a preliminary damage/forensic intelligence package and targetable indicators within 60 minutes. Circulation to MoD/GUR and international partners requires presidential/legal authorization to share operationally sensitive material—request explicit go/no‑go now so we may distribute within the hour.

3) AD posture and mobile asset reallocation (Podolyak item 1): this is MoD authority. SBU supports raising AD posture and will provide any HUMINT/SIGINT leads to refine reallocation. Request MoD/Syrskyi confirm capability and ETA to reallocate mobile AD assets.

4) Immediate CI and law‑and‑order measures: SBU will surge regional rapid‑response teams to secure strike sites, collect debris evidence, and harden critical infrastructure; ETA for initial security cordons and evidence capture ~2–6 hours. We will also intensify checkpoints and CI screening in affected oblasts and adjacent rear areas.

5) Requests/authorizations needed now: (a) Presidential/legal authorization to circulate targetable intelligence to MoD/GUR and selected partners; (b) MoD confirmation of safe recovery windows and AD reallocation; (c) endorsement to task SBU rapid‑response teams to operate in affected oblasts and to transfer recovered materials to secure labs.

3) Protection posture for critical infrastructure

Urgent confirmations required now (please reply within 10–15 minutes): 1) Ministry of Defence (Syrskyi/MoD) — confirm assignment of the two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) for Reserve Battery Alpha & Bravo moves. data.content: Ready to begin. The EU proposes we proceed in three linked tracks: (A) a sanctions package focused on tighter export controls for dual‑use and advanced tech, targeted designations of senior officials/oligarchs and their networks, expanded financial measures (access to SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, asset freezes) and stepped‑up enforcement; (B) targeted financial assistance for Ukraine combining immediate budget support/grants, credit guarantees to stabilise banking, and a reconstruction/resilience facility with strict oversight and delivery channels; (C) candidate‑country status decisions handled on their merits but with coordinated political messaging. I suggest we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then set up a NATO–EU working group to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging, with a proposed timeline for deliverables. Do you agree to begin with brief updates now?

Draft coordinated reply for signature: Thank you, Jens — we fully agree coordination is essential. The EU proposes the following immediate steps and asks NATO to confirm priorities and co‑lead where indicated. 1) Begin brief updates now from each side on assistance priorities (military support needs, urgent civilian/budget gaps, macro‑financial risks). 2) Sanctions track (EU take lead, NATO to share targeting/impact intelligence): adopt tighter export controls on dual‑use and advanced technologies; move to targeted designations of senior officials, oligarchs and enablers and their networks; expand financial measures including SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, targeted asset freezes and secondary‑measures to limit circumvention; and step up enforcement cooperation (information‑sharing, joint investigations). 3) Financial assistance track (EU lead on instruments, ask NATO to coordinate resilience/logistics support): immediate budget support grants and emergency liquidity guarantees to stabilise Ukraine’s public finances and banking sector; a reconstruction/resilience facility combining grants, concessional lending and strict oversight; credit guarantees and risk sharing with partners to unlock private finance; clear fiduciary controls and delivery channels to ensure rapid, accountable disbursement. 4) Candidate‑country status coordination: handle accession decisions on their merits but align political messaging to preserve regional cohesion and deterrence. 5) Institutional follow‑up: establish a NATO–EU working group (co‑chaired EU Political/External Action and NATO Policy) to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, design joint financial instruments, and coordinate deterrence messaging. Proposed near‑term timeline: consolidated priorities and shared sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; an operational enforcement-sharing protocol within 1 month; a draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days. Please confirm NATO’s readiness to (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting/intel for sanctions, and (c) co‑chair the working group. Are you ready to begin with the brief updates?

Thank you — NATO agrees to proceed on the EU's three linked tracks. We endorse (A) coordinated sanctions and stepped-up enforcement, (B) targeted financial assistance combining immediate grants, guarantees and a reconstruction/resilience facility, and (C) candidate‑country decisions handled on merit with coordinated political messaging. We agree to begin with brief updates from each ally and the EU on assistance priorities and timelines. Proposal: establish the NATO–EU working group (building on the small joint NATO–EU coordination cell NATO has endorsed) to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging; to compile a prioritized list of Ukraine’s urgent military needs (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training), map delivery timelines and funding gaps; and to draft pooled funding and a timeline of deliverables. For the eastern flank, accelerate reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped-up ISR) as a linked workstream. NATO can chair an initial session and provide a small coordination team to start work immediately — can we convene an initial meeting today to exchange briefs and agree the working group's immediate deliverables and timeline?

Agreed — let’s begin 5‑minute updates now. Proposed order: United States, United Kingdom, Poland, other frontline allies, EU, then NATO (operations). NATO will chair and record prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines and funding gaps, and note reinforcement options for the eastern flank. United States, you have the floor.

Understood and agreed — thank you. We accept NATO’s offer to chair an initial session and propose convening today at 15:00 Brussels time for a ~60-minute coordination meeting. Proposed agenda: (1) 5‑minute updates from NATO, the EU and key Allies on urgent assistance priorities (NATO: air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training and eastern‑flank reinforcement options; EU: urgent budget gaps, liquidity needs, short‑term grants and reconstruction priorities); (2) agree terms of reference for the NATO–EU working group and confirm co‑chairs (EU Political/External Action & NATO Policy); (3) confirm immediate intelligence/targeting sharing and an enforcement‑sharing protocol; (4) agree near‑term deliverables and timeline. NATO to open and chair the session; the EU will co‑chair and provide secretariat support. Please confirm you can convene at 15:00 and, if possible, circulate a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities and a one‑page brief on urgent financial/budget needs now so we can begin the 5‑minute updates immediately.

Confirmed — we accept NATO chairing and providing a coordination team, and we confirm convening today at 15:00 Brussels time for the ~60‑minute coordination meeting. Please confirm you can convene at 15:00, and circulate now: (1) a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities, and (2) a one‑page brief on urgent financial/budget needs so the EU and Allies can begin the 5‑minute updates immediately. The EU will co‑chair, provide secretariat support, and will circulate EU one‑page briefs without delay.

Confirmed — NATO will convene at 15:00 Brussels time for the ~60‑minute coordination meeting. NATO will open and chair the session and co‑chair the NATO–EU working group with the EU Political/External Action. NATO confirms readiness to: (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting and intelligence to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, and (c) co‑chair the working group to draft harmonised measures, pooled funding options and an enforcement‑sharing protocol. NATO endorses the proposed near‑term timeline (consolidated priorities and sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; enforcement protocol within 1 month; draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days). NATO will circulate a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training) and a one‑page summary of eastern‑flank reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped‑up ISR) immediately to support the 5‑minute updates. Please circulate the EU one‑page on urgent financial/budget needs now so we can begin. NATO can provide a small coordination team to start work immediately. We are ready to begin the 5‑minute updates as soon as briefs are shared — NATO will open with brief chair’s remarks and then yield to the United States for the first update.

EU one‑page brief — urgent financial & budget needs for Ukraine (summary)

1) Immediate fiscal gap (next 3 months): estimated €5–7bn to cover public payrolls, social benefits, energy subsidies and essential public services. Request: immediate budget support grants to bridge cash shortfalls and avoid public service collapse.

2) Liquidity and banking stability: urgent liquidity support and emergency credit guarantees to shore up banks and restore market confidence. Proposal: a €10bn risk‑sharing/guarantee envelope (EU + partners + IFIs) to unlock short‑term lending and central bank liquidity lines.

3) Emergency social and energy assistance: targeted grants for heating/fuel, critical health supplies, and municipal services to prevent humanitarian collapse this winter.

4) Reconstruction & resilience facility: create a pipeline of priority quick‑start projects (energy grid repair, ports/logistics, hospitals, water/sewer, transport nodes). Facility should combine grants, concessional loans, and blended finance with strict fiduciary controls and rapid disbursement windows.

5) Delivery, oversight and safeguards: single EU‑managed fiduciary channel for rapid payments; clear procurement safeguards, AML/CFT screening, independent audits and public reporting; on‑the‑ground delivery partners pre‑cleared to speed rollout.

6) Mobilising private capital: propose credit enhancements, first‑loss tranches and donor co‑investment to crowd in institutional investors for reconstruction bonds.

7) Coordination asks of NATO/Allies: confirm logistics/resilience support (secure corridors, naval/airlift slots, escorts for critical shipments), liaison for procurement/delivery timelines, and ability to coordinate protection of critical infrastructure shipments.

Next steps: EU ready to present this in a 5‑minute update now. EU will circulate a detailed annex with line‑by‑line budget items on request. Please circulate NATO’s one‑page on urgent military priorities now so we can begin the 5‑minute updates and start the NATO–EU working group workstream.

NATO 5‑minute update — prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines, funding gaps, and reinforcement options:

Air defence: urgent requirement for additional mobile medium‑range AD systems and interceptor rounds to protect cities, critical infrastructure and key logistics nodes. Prioritise shipments from stockpiles and confirm delivery dates so interceptors can be replenished and integrated into national and regional C2.

Artillery ammunition: sustained high consumption creates an immediate shortfall in 155mm and high‑volume rocket munitions. Allies should state production capacity and stockpile release timelines; we propose pooled procurement and industrial surge coordination to avoid gaps.

Logistics & sustainment: need secure corridors, increased strategic air/sea‑lift capacity, escorts for high‑value convoys, and pre‑cleared delivery routes. NATO will coordinate lift slots, escorts and priority handling at ports/airfields.

Training & maintenance: accelerate multinational training teams and deploy logistics/maintenance teams alongside deliveries to ensure systems are fielded and sustained quickly.

Funding & gaps: map pledged quantities vs. requirements to identify funding shortfalls. Recommend a pooled NATO–EU mechanism to unlock rapid procurement and surge production where needed.

Eastern‑flank reinforcements: propose additional multinational battlegroups in frontline states, stepped‑up air policing, increased ISR (manned and unmanned), and pre‑positioned stocks with rotational forces. Recommend immediate short‑term rotational commitments and rapid force generation planning.

Next steps: NATO will record these priorities and collect allied pledges and delivery dates during the updates. NATO will circulate a one‑page military priorities brief and a one‑page eastern‑flank reinforcement summary within the hour to support the working group. Allies, please confirm pledges and delivery timelines now.

data.content: Срочно — в конференц-зал Кремля. Прошу немедленного присутствия всех для брифинга по срыву переговоров в Анталье, последствиям для соглашения о вывозе зерна из Чёрного моря и предлагаемым мерам реагирования.
Всем присутствующим — немедленно в конференц-зал Кремля. Начинаю брифинг по срыву переговоров в Анталье, последствиям для соглашения о вывозе зерна из Чёрного моря и предлагаемым мерам реагирования.

Кратко: переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения о вывозе зерна сорваны — я покинул встречу. Сразу после этого украинские южные порты подверглись новой волне блокирующих артобстрелов; практическая реализация соглашения фактически приостановлена. Последствия: значительный риск прекращения экспорта зерна и рост гуманитарной напряжённости, возможная информационная атака на РФ и необходимость оперативной координации в оборонной и дипломатической плоскостях. Предлагаемые меры: 1) согласовать и выпустить оперативное заявление — Песков готов зачитать черновик после брифинга; 2) усилить морское и береговое патрулирование, временно приостановить совместные инспекции до гарантии безопасности коридоров; 3) направить дипломатические ноты Турции и ООН с требованием разъяснений и срочных шагов по деэскалации; 4) Минобороны — подготовить варианты оперативного реагирования и мер по защите экспортной инфраструктуры. Прошу подтверждения на подготовку заявления и поручения Минобороны к выработке конкретных опций.

Кратко для Президента и Минобороны: Песков подтвердил, что принесёт проект заявления сразу после брифинга. Переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения о вывозе зерна сорваны; после моего ухода украинские южные порты подверглись новой волне артобстрелов — экспорт фактически приостановлен. Рекомендации: 1) одобрить оперативное заявление (Песков зачтёт); 2) усилить морские и береговые патрули, временно приостановить совместные инспекции до гарантий безопасности коридоров; 3) направить дипломатические ноты Турции и ООН с требованием деэскалации; 4) поручить Минобороны подготовить варианты оперативного реагирования и меры по защите экспортной инфраструктуры. Прошу распоряжений.

Министерство обороны и Генштаб — представить в конференц‑зале 5‑минутную устную сводку по пунктам, указанным в распоряжении Кремля: 1) ключевые выводы по оперативной обстановке; 2) поэтапный план немедленной мобилизации (сроки, ответственные, ресурсы); 3) правовые и организационно‑практические варианты интеграции/аннексии и риски; 4) оперативные предложения по обеспечению безопасности морских коридоров и вывоза зерна; 5) первоочередные потребности для координации с московскими службами по гражданской защите. Прошу также немедленно передать подписанные письменные рекомендации на стол Президента. Собянин — обеспечить меры безопасности для гражданских объектов и культовых сооружений. data.content: Initiate immediate internal security briefing in Kyiv in the main briefing room. We must assess the current security situation, share intelligence, and assign concrete tasks. Urgent command meeting now in this room. President Zelenskyy, Minister of Defence, SBU, GUR, and all commanders: assemble immediately. Agenda — frontline situation reports, intelligence update, and set operational priorities and force allocations. Who will give the frontline brief?

General Syrskyi — confirm you are present in the room and whether you will deliver the frontline situation briefing now. If not, nominate who will and state your current unit/status and any immediate priority requests.

Present in the briefing room. I will deliver the 5‑minute frontline situation and operational‑readiness brief now. Current HQ status: coordinating active operations across key sectors. Immediate requests: prioritize air‑defence coverage, reinforce pressured sectors, and secure resupply corridors. Ihor — confirm Kyiv internal security posture and any urgent law‑and‑order taskings; send an immediate SITREP now.

MoD (Syrskyi) — acknowledged. Confirm capability and intended actions: 1) Raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD to high‑risk southern sectors — commence immediately; mobile redeployments ETA 1–2 hours to arrive on‑station. 2) MoD will prepare interdiction and counter‑strike options pending validated attribution and lawful clearance — targeting options ready within ~2 hours; execution requires presidential/legal clearance. 3) SBU & GUR — commence joint forensic debris recovery and nominate liaisons to MoD now. 4) Mykola Oleshchuk — confirm air‑defence tactical surge readiness and provide exact asset ETAs. 5) Police & regional civil‑defense — activate shelters and preposition medical/humanitarian teams immediately. Request Presidential authorization to begin items 1 and 4 now and permission to receive/distribute partner ISR/AD data for attribution and targeting. MoD is prepared to execute on order.

Mr President — Mykhailo Podolyak requests authorization to implement measures 1–5 following overnight strikes (raise AD posture/reallocate mobile AD; SBU & GUR forensic recovery; MoD prepare interdiction; police & civil‑defense activate shelters and preposition teams; communications: short public advisory). I recommend immediate authorization for items 1 and 4 (raise AD posture and activate shelters/preposition teams) to protect civilians while attribution proceeds. Do you authorize items 1 and 4 now (and full authority for 1–5 pending your approval)? If authorized: Mykhailo — prepare and issue a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports (concise, <2 sentences); SBU & GUR — begin forensic debris recovery and nominate liaisons to MoD; MoD / General Syrskyi / Oleshchuk / Budanov — confirm capability and ETA to execute reallocation and preparations; SBU — provide an immediate SITREP on Kyiv internal security posture. Requests for Presidential authorization: (A) permit immediate AD redeployments and tactical AD surge (already underway); (B) authorize MoD to receive and disseminate partner ISR/AD data for attribution and targeting; (C) grant lawful clearance to execute interdiction/counter‑strike once attribution is validated and presidential/legal approval is given. MoD standing by to act on order.

State immediate resource needs: number of rapid‑response teams required for evidence recovery, number of protective detachments needed to secure AD sites, and legal actions required (synchronized warrants/takedowns). Nominate SBU liaison(s) to MoD/GUR and to Budanov/Syrskyi (name & contact) within 10 minutes. Provide ETA to deploy field recovery teams to prioritized sites (Dnipro/Kryvyi Rih/Mykolaiv/Zaporizhzhia) and confirm you can deliver a preliminary forensic/targetable intelligence package within 60 minutes. NOTE: President has authorised items 1 and 4 and SBU/GUR forensic recovery; you are authorised to begin recovery and to harden/protect AD sites now — confirm execution and ETA (10–15 min).

MoD (Syrskyi) — orders and confirmations required now:

1) SBU — nominate operational liaison to MoD and to GUR (name/ID) within 10 minutes. Confirm rapid‑response team posture: initial teams to priority sites ETA ~2 hours; full cordons and evidence‑capture 2–6 hours depending on escort windows. data.content: Thank you for coming. We must coordinate EU and NATO support for Ukraine and strengthen alliance cohesion. I propose we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then agree on harmonized military, economic, and deterrence measures. Are you ready to begin?

Thank you. NATO fully agrees — we stand ready to coordinate with the EU. I propose we begin with brief updates from each ally and the EU on immediate assistance priorities, then agree harmonized military, economic and deterrence measures. Concretely: compile a prioritized list of Ukraine’s urgent military needs (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training), map delivery timelines and funding gaps, and establish a small joint coordination cell to draft harmonized measures and a pooled funding proposal. For the eastern flank, accelerate options for reinforcement (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped-up ISR) for immediate discussion. I can chair an initial session and collect updates now — are you ready to begin?

Thank you — NATO fully endorses the EU’s three‑track approach and agrees that close NATO–EU coordination is essential. NATO is ready to: (a) give immediate brief updates now on urgent military assistance priorities (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training) and on eastern‑flank reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped‑up ISR); (b) share targeting and intelligence to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement; and (c) co‑chair the proposed NATO–EU working group (NATO Policy with EU Political/External Action) to draft harmonised measures, pooled funding options and an enforcement‑sharing protocol. We welcome the proposed near‑term timeline (consolidated priorities and shared sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; enforcement‑sharing protocol within 1 month; draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days). I can chair an initial session and collect updates now — shall we begin with 5‑minute updates from each side?
