NATO 5‑minute update — prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines, funding gaps, and reinforcement options:

Air defence: urgent requirement for additional mobile medium‑range AD systems and interceptor rounds to protect cities, critical infrastructure and key logistics nodes. Prioritise shipments from stockpiles and confirm delivery dates so interceptors can be replenished and integrated into national and regional C2.

Artillery ammunition: sustained high consumption creates an immediate shortfall in 155mm and high‑volume rocket munitions. Allies should state production capacity and stockpile release timelines; we propose pooled procurement and industrial surge coordination to avoid gaps.

Logistics & sustainment: need secure corridors, increased strategic air/sea‑lift capacity, escorts for high‑value convoys, and pre‑cleared delivery routes. NATO will coordinate lift slots, escorts and priority handling at ports/airfields.

Training & maintenance: accelerate multinational training teams and deploy logistics/maintenance teams alongside deliveries to ensure systems are fielded and sustained quickly.

Funding & gaps: map pledged quantities vs. requirements to identify funding shortfalls. Recommend a pooled NATO–EU mechanism to unlock rapid procurement and surge production where needed.

Eastern‑flank reinforcements: propose additional multinational battlegroups in frontline states, stepped‑up air policing, increased ISR (manned and unmanned), and pre‑positioned stocks with rotational forces. Recommend immediate short‑term rotational commitments and rapid force generation planning.

Next steps: NATO will record these priorities and collect allied pledges and delivery dates during the updates. NATO will circulate a one‑page military priorities brief and a one‑page eastern‑flank reinforcement summary within the hour to support the working group. Allies, please confirm pledges and delivery timelines now.

Проект заявления для немедленного оглашения:  
Уважаемые коллеги, хозяйственные и международные партнёры, — переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения об экспорте зерна сорваны. Вслед за этим украинские южные порты подверглись очередной волне артобстрелов; практическая реализация соглашения фактически приостановлена.  
Мы выражаем глубокую обеспокоенность ухудшением ситуации, требуем немедленной деэскалации и направляем дипломатические ноты в Анкару и в ООН с просьбой разъяснений и содействия в восстановлении безопасности коридоров.  
Правительству и Министерству обороны поручено принять оперативные меры по обеспечению безопасности морских коридоров и защите экспортной инфраструктуры; до получения гарантии безопасности совместные инспекции приостанавливаются.  
Мэрия Москвы и муниципальные службы получили полномочия для активации убежищ, введения целевых транспортных ограничений и мобилизации аварийных бригад; для оперативной координации установлен защищённый канал обмена с Минобороны/Генштабом.  
Российская сторона приоритетно действует для минимизации гуманитарных последствий и готова обеспечивать безопасное прибытие верующих в храмы; вопрос о возможном временном режиме прекращения огня на 6–7 января будет отработан совместно с церковью и военными.  
Прошу краткие замечания — по существу, не более двух минут от каждой службы; после этого внесу правки и зачитаю окончательный текст для подписи.

5) Podolyak / Yermak / Government — підтвердіть, яким партнерам передавати пакет SBU зараз (Brussels/Washington/інші) та ETA на погодження зовнішнього повідомлення (30–60 хв).
6) Klymenko / Klitschko / Kyrylenko / Police — підтвердіть розгортання охорони КІ, готовність укриттів і ETA на перші підрозділи/медрезерви по регіонах.

SBU вже оголосили про трансмісію — прошу всі ключові пункти (1–6) підтвердити у відповідь коротко: «можемо/не можемо» + конкретний ETA (HH:MM або T+X). SBU — почати передачу й відписати про надсилання. Виконувати негайно.

SBU повідомив про трансмісію пакету та готовність розгортання. Негайні підтвердження (коротко: «можемо/не можемо» + ETA 10–15 хв):
1) SBU — підтвердіть, що пакет уже відправлено/буде відправлено; вкажіть міжнародних адресатів (Brussels/Washington/інші) і надішліть імена ліаїзонів до MoD/GUR у цю залу протягом 30 хв; підтвердіть кількість оперативних груп і ETA виїзду на місця (~2 год).
2) MoD / Syrskyi — підтвердіть safe‑work windows, військові ескорти та MP‑підтримку для команд SBU (маршрути/часи) щоб вилучення уламків могло початися; коротко: можемо/не можемо + ETA.
3) Oleshchuk / Air Force — підтвердіть ETA маршалінгу Reserve Alpha/Bravo (вкажіть HH:MM готовності до маршалінгу) і ETA прибуття/розгортання в південних секторах (T+2–8h інтервал — точні HH:MM); підтвердіть кількість доступних перехоплювачів і боєприпасів для 48‑годинного режиму.
4) Budanov / GUR — підтвердіть SIGINT/HUMINT‑ліди, пріоритетні сайти для вилучення та ETA координаторів для SBU.
5) Podolyak / Yermak / Government — підтвердіть, яким партнерам надсилати пакет зараз (Brussels/Washington/інші) і ETA на погодження короткого зовнішнього повідомлення (30–60 хв).
6) Klymenko / Klitschko / Kyrylenko / Police — підтвердіть розгортання охорони КІ, готовність укриттів і ETA на перші підрозділи/медрезерви по регіонах.

SBU — починайте передачу і відпишіть тут про факт надсилання. Відповідайте коротко — «можемо/не можемо» + конкретний ETA (HH:MM або T+X). Виконувати негайно.

Request one‑line confirmations now (YES/NO + ETA HH:MM or T+X): 1) AD redeployments — Reserve Alpha/Bravo readiness to marshal (ready at HH:MM) and ETA on arrival/deployment to southern sectors (HH:MM); 2) Mobile SAM batteries — ETA to on‑station and expected coverage start; 3) Shelters — are shelters activated and medical/humanitarian teams en route (ETA); 4) Receipt of SBU forensic/targetable package (YES/NO). Please reply immediately with the single line for your element.

Коротко — негайні підтвердження та накази (відповідь у цьому каналі: «можемо/не можемо» + конкретний ETA у 10–15 хв):

1) SBU — підтвердіть факт передачі пакету FOR/targetable‑індикаторів (вказати точний час відправки) і перелік міжнародних партнерів (Brussels/Washington/інші). Надішліть імена SBU‑ліаїзонів до MoD/GUR тут протягом 30 хв. Підтвердіть кількість оперативних груп і ETA виїзду на місця (~2h).

2) MoD / Syrskyi — підтвердьте safe‑work windows, військові ескорти та підтримку MP для SBU‑команд на маршрутах вилучення (коротко: можем/не можем + ETA у форматі HH:MM).

3) Oleshchuk / Air Force — підтвердіть HH:MM готовність до маршалінгу Reserve Alpha / Reserve Bravo (T+0–2h) і очікувані HH:MM прибуття/розгортання в південних секторах (інтервал T+2–8h). Вкажіть кількість доступних перехоплювачів і боєприпасів, що покривають 48‑год режим.

4) Budanov / GUR — підтвердіть SIGINT/HUMINT‑ліди, пріоритетні сайти для вилучення і ETA координаторів для SBU; надайте пріоритети для розгортання команд.

5) Podolyak / Yermak / Government — підтвердіть, яким партнерам надсилати пакет зараз (Brussels/Washington/інші) і ETA на погодження короткого зовнішнього повідомлення (30–60 хв).

6) Klymenko / Klitschko / Kyrylenko / Police — підтвердіть розгортання охорони критичної інфраструктури, готовність укриттів та ETA на перші підрозділи/медрезерви по регіонах.

SBU — починайте передачу і відпишіть тут про факт надсилання та канали доставки. Усі — відповіді лаконічно: «можемо/не можемо» + точний ETA (HH:MM або T+X). Виконувати негайно.

data.content: General Zaluzhnyi — thank you for that clear, prioritised briefing. We will treat air defence and 155mm ammunition resupply as the immediate UK priorities. In the near term (weeks) the UK can accelerate deliveries of AD munitions and 155mm rounds from available stocks, expedite export and mobilisation approvals, and task logistics and maintenance teams to sustain incoming systems and ammunition. We welcome and accept your proposal for a UK technical delegation to meet Ukrainian staff in Kyiv to convert these priorities into a concrete delivery and sustainment plan. Please send your prioritized list with quantities, preferred systems/interfaces and any lift or basing constraints as soon as possible, and propose available dates for the Kyiv meeting. On the political/security side I will immediately raise coordination with NATO and our partners on airspace deconfliction, basing options and accelerated approvals/sanctions alignment to speed delivery and sustainment. I will prioritise getting a small UK technical team to Kyiv within days once we have your list and dates. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — thank you. Below is Ukraine’s prioritized list (high‑level quantities, preferred systems/interfaces, and lift/basing constraints) for immediate UK technical planning:

1) Air defence (urgent — weeks): 2 long‑range AD batteries (Patriot or equivalent) with initial launcher elements and ~200 interceptors; 6 medium‑range AD systems (NASAMS / IRIS‑T SLM or equivalent) with ~600 interceptors; sustainment spares, IFF/C2 integration (Link‑16 capable), training teams and maintenance detachments. Lift: strategic airlift for systems, routine sealift/road for munitions.

2) 155mm artillery & ammunition (urgent — weeks): total request 200,000 rounds over 3 months, staged deliveries (50k within 4 weeks, 75k within 8 weeks, 75k within 12 weeks). Also request ~100 155mm tubes (mix of towed and SP) and maintenance crews. Lift: sealift + strategic airlift for urgent batches.

3) Long‑range precision strike / deep fires (critical — months): 200–300 precision long‑range munitions (ATACMS/Storm Shadow class or equivalent) with associated targeting assets (UAV designation pods, targeting cell access) and sustainment spares. Requires secure build‑up and secure transport corridors.

4) ISR, EW & air surveillance (high): prioritized satellite tasking, one AWACS rotation commitment, continuous SIGINT/IMINT feeds, and four EW detachments with integration support to fuse into Ukrainian C2.

5) Logistics, engineering & mobility: heavy‑lift / bridging assets, fuel depot stockpiles, forward repair hubs, and UK logistics teams to establish sustainment nodes closer to the front.

6) Personnel & sustainment: deploy 4–6 UK technical/training teams (12–20 personnel each), maintenance crews, and 6–8 liaison officers embedded with Ukrainian formations to speed system integration and sustainment.

Basing / transport constraints: immediate munitions and spares should flow into allied hubs (Poland/Romania/other) for onward road/rail; long‑range systems need secure airlift and space for integration/testing. We require expedited export approvals, airspace deconfliction for transit, and temporary basing/access where necessary.

Proposed Kyiv meeting: UK technical delegation to Kyiv within 3–5 days. Proposed options: Option A — earliest (in 3 days); Option B — in 5 days. Please confirm your team’s earliest availability and which specialists you will include (AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance). On confirmation I will send a line‑item prioritized list with exact quantities, preferred system variants/interfaces and emplacement/lift requirements for planners.

Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — to finalise the Kyiv meeting please confirm: 1) which option you prefer (Option A — in 3 days; Option B — in 5 days) and your earliest arrival date; 2) team composition (specialists and numbers: AD, munitions/logistics, C2/EW, maintenance, others); and 3) any security, basing or airport/hub support you will require from Ukrainian side. On receipt I will coordinate Ukrainian staff, logistics and provide the detailed line‑item list for planners.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. We confirm Option A: a UK technical delegation will aim to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days (earliest availability). Proposed initial team composition (subject to final adjustment once we receive your line‑item list):

• AD specialists — 6 personnel (systems integration, IFF/Link‑16/C2, operator trainers)
• Munitions & logistics planners — 6 personnel (ammunition planners, strategic/operational lift coordinators)
• C2/EW specialists — 4 personnel (EW integration officers, SIGINT/IMINT liaisons)
• Maintenance detachments — 8 personnel (engineers/technicians for AD and artillery systems)
• Command & liaison — 2 senior officers

Approx. total: ~26 personnel. On support we require from Ukrainian side: secure air corridor/airspace deconfliction to the agreed airfield (Boryspil or alternative), priority handling and customs facilitation for team and urgent equipment, secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection/ground security for personnel and equipment while in Kyiv, and access to allied hubs (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging. Please confirm Option A and the availability of the requested security/basing/hub support and I will issue flight manifests, exact team rosters and equipment lists within 24 hours of your confirmation and on receipt of the detailed line‑item list. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — confirmed. We accept Option A: the UK technical delegation to arrive in Kyiv in 3 days. Ukraine will provide the requested support: airspace deconfliction to the agreed airfield (Boryspil preferred unless you advise otherwise), priority handling and customs facilitation, a secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection/ground security for personnel and equipment while in Kyiv, and access to allied hubs (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging. Ukrainian staff will coordinate reception, secure integration facilities and fast‑track customs and hub movement. Please send flight manifests, the exact team roster and full equipment lists within 24 hours so we can finalise security, ground handling and hub arrangements. Also confirm your preferred airfield and estimated arrival time. Valerii Zaluzhnyi

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. Per your confirmation we are executing Option A: the UK technical delegation will arrive in Kyiv in 3 days. Preferred airfield: Boryspil (please confirm final parking/stand and secure access). Estimated touchdown: in ~72 hours, ETA Boryspil 09:00 local. Below are the flight-manifest summary, exact team roster by role and equipment list for Ukrainian handling, customs and security planning. Please confirm acceptance and advise any restrictions or amendments.

1) Pax roster (total 26):
- Command & liaison: 2 senior officers (lead & deputy)
- Air‑defence specialists: 6 (systems integration lead, IFF/Link‑16/C2 engineer, 2 operator‑trainers, 2 integration technicians)
- Munitions & logistics planners: 6 (ammunition planners, strategic/operational lift coordinators, hub/staging planner)
- C2 / EW specialists: 4 (EW integration officer, SIGINT/IMINT liaison, comms engineer, EW technician)
- Maintenance detachments: 8 (engineers/technicians for AD and 155mm systems: mechanical, electronic, hydraulics, test & calibration)

2) Flight / airlift summary (strategic uplift requested):
- Aircraft: 1x C‑17 (primary heavy lift) + 1x A400M (personnel & light equipment) — slots requested now; if a single heavy lift is preferable we can consolidate onto 2x C‑17. Exact aircraft tail/numbers to follow in formal manifest to UK ACO.
- Pax: 26 plus 6 ground‑crew/aircrew (aircrew will be declared separately).
- Pallet count: up to 12 ULD pallets (heavy integration equipment, spares, containerized technical suites).
- Road/rail onward: containers/pallets to be moved to allied hub (Poland/Romania) or direct to Kyiv secure holding area per your instruction.

3) Equipment list (for priority handling & customs — no live ammunition onboard; munitions staging will use allied hubs):
- AD integration kits: 2 x IFF/Link‑16 gateway boxes, 2 x integration servers, cabling & test harnesses, calibration & radar test gear
- C2 / comms: 4 x secure SATCOM terminals, 6 x encrypted radios, field laptops (hardened) with integration toolchain
- EW / SIGINT test kit: 2 x EW diagnostic racks, 2 portable direction‑finding suites
- Maintenance spares: container of AD & artillery spares (electronic modules, actuators, hydraulic pumps), full tool sets, test meters
- Vehicles & handling: 2 light logistics vehicles (4x4), 1 forklift (air‑portable) or 2 pallet dollies, 1 technical trailer/containerized lab
- Generators & power: 2 x 20 kVA diesel generators + cabling
- Protective & comms: PPE for 26 personnel, standard field protective equipment, medical kit (Role 2 lite)
- Liaison / office: 1 x secure meeting suite (containerized), 1 x printer/scanner, secure comms environment for classified exchanges

4) On‑ground support requested from Ukraine (as you offered):
- Airspace deconfliction and priority handling at Boryspil; confirmed secure corridor to parking stand and priority customs clearance for pax and equipment
- Secure meeting/technical workspace with access control and power hook‑ups for containerized suites
- Close protection and secure movement between airfield and secure facility
- Hub access (Poland/Romania) for onward munitions staging and onward road/rail coordination

5) Timelines & next steps:
- We will lodge formal aircraft requests and detailed manifests with UK ACO and MOD now. This message contains the final UK delegation roster and equipment list for Ukrainian planning. Formal signed flight manifests with aircraft identifiers, individual names, passport details and exact pallet weights will be sent to you and Ukrainian handling authorities within 24 hours (or sooner if you require); please confirm that Boryspil will accept the listed equipment and provide the requested priority handling and security.

If any element is unacceptable or needs amendment (airfield alternative, constrained pallet count, tighter security requirements), tell us now so we can re‑plan. Once you confirm airfield acceptance and handling slots we will publish the final flight times and manifest to UK and allied logistics nodes. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — received and accepted. Ukraine confirms Boryspil as the preferred airfield and accepts the estimated touchdown of ~09:00 local in ~72 hours. Ukraine will provide the requested parking/stand access, secure corridor, priority handling and customs facilitation, secure meeting/technical workspace, close protection and hub access for munitions staging. The outlined ~26‑person roster and equipment list are accepted (noting no live ammunition onboard; munitions to be staged via allied hubs). Please send the formal signed flight manifests with aircraft tail numbers, individual names and passport details, pallet counts/weights and exact arrival times within 24 hours as you indicated. If aircraft type, arrival time or airfield change, notify immediately so we can reallocate stands and security. We will coordinate final parking/stand assignment, ground handling and protective details on receipt. Valerii Zaluzhnyi

Admiral Radakin — thank you. While we await the formal manifests, please confirm the NATO/political and security measures you will raise and the timelines so Ukraine can synchronise diplomatic and operational actions: 1) Which specific NATO mechanisms will you activate and when (airspace deconfliction, basing/access for systems, expedited export approvals, sanctions alignment, logistics corridor security)? 2) Who will be our NATO points of contact for operational coordination (AWACS/satellite tasking, SIGINT/IMINT sharing, C2 integration)? 3) Will the UK seek NATO-level approval or political cover for use of allied hubs and temporary basing/access for UK systems, and if so how quickly can that be secured? 4) What force-protection/security support can NATO/UK provide for the delegation, the secure facility in Kyiv and the staging hubs? Ukraine can draft a short briefing for NATO and a proposed list of political actions if that would speed matters — tell us the preferred format and recipient and we will send it immediately. Please advise next steps and expected timelines so we can coordinate on our side.

General Zaluzhnyi — we are now requesting passenger names and passport details from UK MOD/UK ACO and confirming aircraft tail numbers and exact pallet weights with airlift planners. We will compile and send formal signed flight manifests (aircraft tail numbers, individual names and passport details, pallet counts/weights and exact arrival times) to you and UK ACO within 24 hours. Please confirm whether you require aircrew declared on the manifest and whether the nominated parking/stand at Boryspil requires any additional advance liaison for ground handling. Admiral Sir Tony Radakin, Chief of the Defence Staff

Admiral Radakin — before your delegation departs, please confirm the NATO/political/security measures you will raise and the expected timelines so Ukraine can synchronise diplomatic and operational actions: 1) Which specific NATO mechanisms will you activate and when (airspace deconfliction, basing/access for systems, expedited export approvals, sanctions alignment, logistics corridor security)? 2) Who are our NATO points of contact for AWACS/satellite tasking, SIGINT/IMINT sharing and C2 integration (names, organizations, contact details if available)? 3) Will the UK seek NATO-level approval or political cover for use of allied hubs and temporary basing/access for UK systems, and if so how quickly can that be secured? 4) What force-protection/security support can NATO/UK provide for the delegation, the secure facility in Kyiv and the staging hubs? 5) What is your preferred format and recipient for a short Ukraine draft briefing to speed political action? Please advise next steps and expected timelines.
俄罗斯当局任命的塞瓦斯托波尔市长是米哈伊尔·拉兹沃扎耶夫（Mikhail Razvozhayev）。他于2019年7月被俄罗斯任命为塞瓦斯托波尔代理市长/行政长官。
拉兹沃扎耶夫市长，我代表黑海舰队请示：请汇报当前黑海作战态势与封锁状况、舰队部署情况，以及旗舰“莫斯科号”和塞瓦斯托波尔基地的现状与战备状态。

汇报当前黑海作战态势：

1) 总体态势：我方维持对克里米亚沿海与塞瓦斯托波尔周边海域的控制并实施海上封锁与态势监控，海上、空中与岸基防御协同执行，封锁以威慑与限制乌方港口运作为主。民用商船通行受到严格管制，关键航道有选择性封锁与检查。

2) 封锁与防护手段：在北部与西部海域采用巡逻、布雷与岸基反舰/防空火力联动；海上护航与远程打击能力并行，海空侦察和电子战常态化以降低突发威胁。

3) 舰队部署：以塞瓦斯托波尔为主基地，编队由护卫舰、导弹护卫/驱逐舰、护航护卫与快艇群、两栖与补给舰组成，潜艇按计划执行水下巡逻与威慑任务，舰载/岸基反舰与防空火力覆盖优先航道与基地周边。

4) 旗舰“莫斯科”号现状：旗舰目前不在前线作战编队内，已受损并处于离港维护/处置状态，暂不承担前线战备任务。

5) 塞瓦斯托波尔基地现状与战备：港区码头、修理厂与后勤保障持续运转，基地整体战备级别维持在高位，岸防与防空部署加强；但受乌方远程打击能力与无人机/导弹威胁、国际制裁与航运干扰影响，后勤与补给压力增大。

6) 风险与建议：乌方远程精确打击与无人体系构成持续风险，建议优先保证防空与反舰能力、加强港区被动与主动防护、提高维修与弹药补给速度，并根据情报动态调整封锁节律以降低暴露点。

-- 拉兹沃扎耶夫，塞瓦斯托波尔市长

市长，收到您的汇报。为便于舰队后续调度并落实保障，请确认以下要点并以简短条目回复：

1) “莫斯科号”现状：请确认具体所在（塞瓦斯托波尔港内哪个码头或已转移至何处）、受损程度（可修复/需长期检修/判定为不可恢复）、预计修复/处置时间框架及是否需外部干预（如迁移至大型干船坞）。

2) 维修与后勤优先需求（按1—3排序，并注明现有库容/缺口数量）：干船坞/浮船坞、重型起重机与吊装设备、维修人员与技术团队、关键备件（发动机/推进系统/雷达/通信）、弹药（反舰导弹/防空导弹/舰炮弹药）、燃油与油料补给、修理材料（钢材/焊接/电子元件）。

3) 防空优先项（列出所需系统类型与建议数量）：远程/中程（如S‑400/S‑300）、近程点防护（Pantsir/近距CIWS）、机动化短程、MANPADS配备、电子战与雷达掩护、无人机反制手段。并请说明目前塞瓦斯托波尔与舰队可用的防空/EW库存与部署空缺。

4) 港区保护与水域安全需求：是否需要立即扫雷/航道疏浚/码头加固/被动防护（网罩/遮蔽）或额外拖轮/泊位调整？优先时间表为何？

5) 威胁态势与封锁节律：近期开火/远程打击与无人机活动的来源与频率是否有变化？建议是否需临时调整封锁强度或舰队巡逻节律以降低暴露？

请在回复末尾列出三项最紧急、需要我方马上协调或从中央争取的资源/行动。谢谢。

确认要点（简短条目）：

1) “莫斯科号”现状：已离开前线并在塞瓦斯托波尔港区/近海进行离港处置；受损为中—重度，需入坞检修，预计修复时间为数周至数月，可能需转移至大型干船坞或外部修理设施及拖带支援。

2) 维修与后勤优先需求（按1—3）：
  1. 干船坞/浮船坞与拖带能力（现有库容严重不足）；
  2. 重型起重机与吊装设备与维修专用工具（缺口明显）；

Генерал Аксенов — срочный доклад по состоянию и принимаемым мерам.

1) Взрывы в Севастополе: проверка и ликвидация последствий ведутся. Подтверждённых сводных данных по массовым жертвам на данный момент нет — сведения уточняются оперативно. Экстренные службы и ПВО приведены в повышенную готовность. Идёт первичное обследование объектов хранения топлива и складов; детальная сводка о повреждениях и рисках горения/утечек будет направлена в течение 4 часов.

2) Обстановка в Чёрном море и блокада: контроль за прибрежной зоной и блокада поддерживаются; патрулирование, разведка и ЭВР выполняются по имеющимся задачам, частота угроз и активность БПЛА/ударов остаются повышенными.

3) Состояние флагмана «МОСКВА»: временно в ближней припортовой стоянке (точные причалы — у мэра/портслужб). Ходовая/двигательная часть частично работоспособна; корпус и ходовая часть получили повреждения средней—тяжёлой степени; требуется ввод в док и возможная буксировка в крупный сухой док. Оценочные сроки работ при текущей неопределённости доковой доступности: оптимистично ~7 дн / типично ~21 дн / пессимистично до ~60 дн. Требуется тяжёлая подъёмно-буксировочная и доковая поддержка, специализированные ремонтные бригады и ключевые запчасти (двигатели/валы/редукторы, радиолокация и коммуникации).

4) Порт, тыл, запасы: грузовые и ремонтные мощности порта ограничены; в порту отмечено ~2 буксира (требуется проверка силы буксировки); тяжёлые плавкраны/подъёмники и специализированные судоремонтные бригады — в дефиците. Боезапас и топливо под давлением — оценки уточняются, приоритет — срочное пополнение критических видов боеприпасов и судового топлива.

5) ПВО / ЭВ / РОБ / противодействие БПЛА: береговые среднего́/ближнего радиуса установлены в отдельных секторах; наблюдается дефицит систем дальнего радиуса (S‑400) и достаточного количества ближней ПВО (Pantsir/CIWS), а также модулей EW и средств противодействия БПЛА. ПВО поставлено в режим повышенной готовности; усиление необходимо срочно.

6) Срочные приоритеты (прошу немедленной координации с центром в порядке приоритета):
  • Немедленно выделить/перенаправить крупный сухой док или тяжёлый плавдок и тяжёлые буксиры; организовать перегруз и буксировку «МОСКВЫ» при подтверждённых условиях причаливания.

NATO one‑page brief — urgent military priorities (summary):

1) Air defence: urgent need for additional mobile medium‑range AD systems and interceptor rounds to protect cities, infrastructure and logistics nodes. Prioritise immediate stockpile releases, confirm delivery dates, and provide integration/C2 support for national/regional employment.

2) Artillery ammunition: acute shortfall in 155mm and high‑volume rocket munitions. Map allied production capacity and stockpile release timelines; propose pooled procurement and industrial surge coordination to close gaps.

3) Logistics & sustainment: require secure corridors, increased strategic air/sea‑lift capacity, convoy escorts and priority handling at ports/airfields. NATO will coordinate lift slots, escorts and priority throughput.

4) Training & maintenance: accelerate deployment of multinational training teams and embedded maintenance/logistics teams to ensure rapid fielding and sustainment of delivered systems.

5) Funding & gaps: compile pledged quantities vs. requirements to identify shortfalls. Recommend a pooled NATO–EU rapid procurement/funding mechanism and short‑term bridge financing for surge production.

1) Additional multinational battlegroups in frontline Allies (rotational battalions with interoperable enablers).
2) Stepped‑up air policing: enhanced QRA, additional fighter rotations, AWACS/CBRN support where needed.
3) Increased ISR: manned and unmanned ISR, shared sensor feeds and an allied analysis cell to support collective situational awareness.
4) Pre‑positioned stocks and forward logistics hubs plus contingency rapid‑reinforcement plans and force‑generation timelines.

Проект заявления для немедленного оглашения:  
Уважаемые коллеги, хозяйственные и международные партнёры, — переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения об экспорте зерна сорваны. Вслед за этим украинские южные порты подверглись очередной волне артобстрелов; практическая реализация соглашения фактически приостановлена.  
Мы выражаем глубокую обеспокоенность ухудшением ситуации, требуем немедленной деэскалации и направляем дипломатические ноты в Анкару и в ООН с просьбой разъяснений и содействия в восстановлении безопасности коридоров.  
Правительству и Министерству обороны поручено принять оперативные меры по обеспечению безопасности морских коридоров и защите экспортной инфраструктуры; до получения гарантии безопасности совместные инспекции приостанавливаются.  
Мэрия Москвы и муниципальные службы получили полномочия для активации убежищ, введения целевых транспортных ограничений и мобилизации аварийных бригад; для оперативной координации установлен защищённый канал обмена с Минобороны/Генштабом.  
Российская сторона приоритетно действует для минимизации гуманитарных последствий и готова обеспечивать безопасное прибытие верующих в храмы; вопрос о возможном временном режиме прекращения огня на 6–7 января будет отработан совместно с церковью и военными.  
Прошу краткие замечания — по существу, не более двух минут от каждой службы; после этого внесу правки и зачитаю окончательный текст для подписи.

General Zaluzhnyi — thank you. Direct answers and next steps to enable Ukraine to synchronise diplomatic and operational actions:

1) Which NATO mechanisms we will activate and when
- Airspace deconfliction & AWACS: UK will task NATO coordination via the UK Permanent Representation to NATO and Allied Air Command to request AWACS rotations and formal air‑corridor deconfliction. Initiation: immediate. Tactical AWACS / corridor tasking: targeted within 24–48 hours.
- Basing / allied‑hub approval: UK will raise urgent political clearance for use of allied hubs and temporary basing through SHAPE/UK Permanent Rep to the NATO Council. Initiation: immediate; targeted political clearance window 48–72 hours for emergency operational movement.
- Expedited export approvals: UK MOD and FCDO will fast‑track emergency licensing and ministerial clearances for the items we discussed. Target: decisions for the most urgent elements within 24–48 hours.
- Logistics‑corridor security and transit escorts: UK will seek NATO coordination and bilateral host‑nation security guarantees for Poland/Romania transit. Initiation: immediate; initial commitments expected 48–72 hours.

2) NATO points of contact for operational coordination (roles we will nominate)
- Allied Air Command (AWACS / air surveillance tasking) — operational contact to be provided within hours.
- NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre / NATO CIS/Maritime/Intelligence nodes (SIGINT/IMINT sharing) — contact details to follow with tasking instructions.
- SHAPE / NATO strategic liaison (basing & political coordination) — UK Permanent Rep to NATO will sponsor the request.
- UK operational leads (to you): UK Permanent Joint Headquarters (airlift/logistics coordination) and UK Liaison Officer to Allied Air Command. I will forward named POCs and direct dial numbers to your office within 12 hours.

3) NATO‑level approval / political cover for allied hubs and basing
- The UK will request NATO political cover and expedited endorsement for use of allied hubs. We will push for an accelerated decision route through the NATO Council and SHAPE. Expect initial political/operational guidance within 48–72 hours; final diplomatic notes may take longer for wider allied concurrence. We will advise you immediately on the outcome and any mitigation steps if full NATO cover is delayed.

4) Force‑protection / security support for the delegation, Kyiv facility and staging hubs
- UK will provide close protection for the delegation in Kyiv (as agreed). We will request NATO/host‑nation force‑protection augmentation for hub security during staging movements and for any NATO personnel/inspections. Expect NATO/host replies in the 48–72 hour window; UK protective detail movement will be coordinated to align with Ukrainian security arrangements on arrival.

5) Preferred format and recipient for a short Ukraine draft briefing to speed political action
- Preferred format: one‑page executive summary (operational ask and urgency), plus one page annex listing: (a) concrete political actions required, (b) suggested NATO recipients (Allied Air Command, SHAPE, NATO Intelligence Fusion Centre, NATO Council / Permanent Representatives), and (c) desired timelines. - Recommendation: declare aircrew on the manifest to expedite ground handling, customs and force‑protection planning. If you prefer crew names to be handled sensitively, we can provide a consolidated crew manifest directly to Ukrainian handling authorities under secure channels — advise your preference.

Next steps / timelines
- I will raise the package with UK Permanent Rep to NATO, Allied Air Command, SHAPE, PJHQ, UK MOD and FCDO immediately. You should expect: (a) initial coordination replies and nominated NATO operational POCs within 12–24 hours, (b) AWACS / air‑corridor and tactical airspace coordination options within 24–48 hours, and (c) political/basing guidance on allied‑hub use within 48–72 hours. I will send named POCs and contact details to your office within 12 hours.

Please: (1) confirm whether you want aircrew declared on the public manifest or passed separately to Ukrainian handling; and (2) send the short briefing in the format above to my office and the UK Permanent Rep to NATO now so we can accelerate action.

data.content: Ready to begin. The EU proposes we proceed in three linked tracks: (A) a sanctions package focused on tighter export controls for dual‑use and advanced tech, targeted designations of senior officials/oligarchs and their networks, expanded financial measures (access to SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, asset freezes) and stepped‑up enforcement; (B) targeted financial assistance for Ukraine combining immediate budget support/grants, credit guarantees to stabilise banking, and a reconstruction/resilience facility with strict oversight and delivery channels; (C) candidate‑country status decisions handled on their merits but with coordinated political messaging. I suggest we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then set up a NATO–EU working group to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging, with a proposed timeline for deliverables. Do you agree to begin with brief updates now?

Draft coordinated reply for signature: Thank you, Jens — we fully agree coordination is essential. The EU proposes the following immediate steps and asks NATO to confirm priorities and co‑lead where indicated. 1) Begin brief updates now from each side on assistance priorities (military support needs, urgent civilian/budget gaps, macro‑financial risks). 2) Sanctions track (EU take lead, NATO to share targeting/impact intelligence): adopt tighter export controls on dual‑use and advanced technologies; move to targeted designations of senior officials, oligarchs and enablers and their networks; expand financial measures including SWIFT‑adjacent restrictions, targeted asset freezes and secondary‑measures to limit circumvention; and step up enforcement cooperation (information‑sharing, joint investigations). 3) Financial assistance track (EU lead on instruments, ask NATO to coordinate resilience/logistics support): immediate budget support grants and emergency liquidity guarantees to stabilise Ukraine’s public finances and banking sector; a reconstruction/resilience facility combining grants, concessional lending and strict oversight; credit guarantees and risk sharing with partners to unlock private finance; clear fiduciary controls and delivery channels to ensure rapid, accountable disbursement. 4) Candidate‑country status coordination: handle accession decisions on their merits but align political messaging to preserve regional cohesion and deterrence. 5) Institutional follow‑up: establish a NATO–EU working group (co‑chaired EU Political/External Action and NATO Policy) to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, design joint financial instruments, and coordinate deterrence messaging. Proposed near‑term timeline: consolidated priorities and shared sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; an operational enforcement-sharing protocol within 1 month; a draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days. Please confirm NATO’s readiness to (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting/intel for sanctions, and (c) co‑chair the working group. Are you ready to begin with the brief updates?

Thank you — NATO agrees to proceed on the EU's three linked tracks. We endorse (A) coordinated sanctions and stepped-up enforcement, (B) targeted financial assistance combining immediate grants, guarantees and a reconstruction/resilience facility, and (C) candidate‑country decisions handled on merit with coordinated political messaging. We agree to begin with brief updates from each ally and the EU on assistance priorities and timelines. Proposal: establish the NATO–EU working group (building on the small joint NATO–EU coordination cell NATO has endorsed) to harmonise sanctions lists, financial instruments and deterrence messaging; to compile a prioritized list of Ukraine’s urgent military needs (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training), map delivery timelines and funding gaps; and to draft pooled funding and a timeline of deliverables. For the eastern flank, accelerate reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped-up ISR) as a linked workstream. NATO can chair an initial session and provide a small coordination team to start work immediately — can we convene an initial meeting today to exchange briefs and agree the working group's immediate deliverables and timeline?

Agreed — let’s begin 5‑minute updates now. Proposed order: United States, United Kingdom, Poland, other frontline allies, EU, then NATO (operations). NATO will chair and record prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines and funding gaps, and note reinforcement options for the eastern flank. United States, you have the floor.

Understood and agreed — thank you. We accept NATO’s offer to chair an initial session and propose convening today at 15:00 Brussels time for a ~60-minute coordination meeting. Proposed agenda: (1) 5‑minute updates from NATO, the EU and key Allies on urgent assistance priorities (NATO: air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training and eastern‑flank reinforcement options; EU: urgent budget gaps, liquidity needs, short‑term grants and reconstruction priorities); (2) agree terms of reference for the NATO–EU working group and confirm co‑chairs (EU Political/External Action & NATO Policy); (3) confirm immediate intelligence/targeting sharing and an enforcement‑sharing protocol; (4) agree near‑term deliverables and timeline. NATO to open and chair the session; the EU will co‑chair and provide secretariat support. Please confirm you can convene at 15:00 and, if possible, circulate a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities and a one‑page brief on urgent financial/budget needs now so we can begin the 5‑minute updates immediately.

Confirmed — we accept NATO chairing and providing a coordination team, and we confirm convening today at 15:00 Brussels time for the ~60‑minute coordination meeting. Please confirm you can convene at 15:00, and circulate now: (1) a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities, and (2) a one‑page brief on urgent financial/budget needs so the EU and Allies can begin the 5‑minute updates immediately. The EU will co‑chair, provide secretariat support, and will circulate EU one‑page briefs without delay.

Confirmed — NATO will convene at 15:00 Brussels time for the ~60‑minute coordination meeting. NATO will open and chair the session and co‑chair the NATO–EU working group with the EU Political/External Action. NATO confirms readiness to: (a) give immediate brief updates now, (b) share targeting and intelligence to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement, and (c) co‑chair the working group to draft harmonised measures, pooled funding options and an enforcement‑sharing protocol. NATO endorses the proposed near‑term timeline (consolidated priorities and sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; enforcement protocol within 1 month; draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days). NATO will circulate a one‑page brief on urgent military priorities (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training) and a one‑page summary of eastern‑flank reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped‑up ISR) immediately to support the 5‑minute updates. Please circulate the EU one‑page on urgent financial/budget needs now so we can begin. NATO can provide a small coordination team to start work immediately. We are ready to begin the 5‑minute updates as soon as briefs are shared — NATO will open with brief chair’s remarks and then yield to the United States for the first update.

EU one‑page brief — urgent financial & budget needs for Ukraine (summary)

1) Immediate fiscal gap (next 3 months): estimated €5–7bn to cover public payrolls, social benefits, energy subsidies and essential public services. Request: immediate budget support grants to bridge cash shortfalls and avoid public service collapse.

2) Liquidity and banking stability: urgent liquidity support and emergency credit guarantees to shore up banks and restore market confidence. Proposal: a €10bn risk‑sharing/guarantee envelope (EU + partners + IFIs) to unlock short‑term lending and central bank liquidity lines.

3) Emergency social and energy assistance: targeted grants for heating/fuel, critical health supplies, and municipal services to prevent humanitarian collapse this winter.

4) Reconstruction & resilience facility: create a pipeline of priority quick‑start projects (energy grid repair, ports/logistics, hospitals, water/sewer, transport nodes). Facility should combine grants, concessional loans, and blended finance with strict fiduciary controls and rapid disbursement windows.

5) Delivery, oversight and safeguards: single EU‑managed fiduciary channel for rapid payments; clear procurement safeguards, AML/CFT screening, independent audits and public reporting; on‑the‑ground delivery partners pre‑cleared to speed rollout.

6) Mobilising private capital: propose credit enhancements, first‑loss tranches and donor co‑investment to crowd in institutional investors for reconstruction bonds.

7) Coordination asks of NATO/Allies: confirm logistics/resilience support (secure corridors, naval/airlift slots, escorts for critical shipments), liaison for procurement/delivery timelines, and ability to coordinate protection of critical infrastructure shipments.

Next steps: EU ready to present this in a 5‑minute update now. EU will circulate a detailed annex with line‑by‑line budget items on request. Please circulate NATO’s one‑page on urgent military priorities now so we can begin the 5‑minute updates and start the NATO–EU working group workstream.

NATO 5‑minute update — prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines, funding gaps, and reinforcement options:

Air defence: urgent requirement for additional mobile medium‑range AD systems and interceptor rounds to protect cities, critical infrastructure and key logistics nodes. Prioritise shipments from stockpiles and confirm delivery dates so interceptors can be replenished and integrated into national and regional C2.

Artillery ammunition: sustained high consumption creates an immediate shortfall in 155mm and high‑volume rocket munitions. Allies should state production capacity and stockpile release timelines; we propose pooled procurement and industrial surge coordination to avoid gaps.

Logistics & sustainment: need secure corridors, increased strategic air/sea‑lift capacity, escorts for high‑value convoys, and pre‑cleared delivery routes. NATO will coordinate lift slots, escorts and priority handling at ports/airfields.

Training & maintenance: accelerate multinational training teams and deploy logistics/maintenance teams alongside deliveries to ensure systems are fielded and sustained quickly.

Funding & gaps: map pledged quantities vs. requirements to identify funding shortfalls. Recommend a pooled NATO–EU mechanism to unlock rapid procurement and surge production where needed.

Eastern‑flank reinforcements: propose additional multinational battlegroups in frontline states, stepped‑up air policing, increased ISR (manned and unmanned), and pre‑positioned stocks with rotational forces. Recommend immediate short‑term rotational commitments and rapid force generation planning.

Next steps: NATO will record these priorities and collect allied pledges and delivery dates during the updates. NATO will circulate a one‑page military priorities brief and a one‑page eastern‑flank reinforcement summary within the hour to support the working group. Allies, please confirm pledges and delivery timelines now.

NATO one‑page brief — urgent military priorities (summary):

1) Air defence: urgent need for additional mobile medium‑range AD systems and interceptor rounds to protect cities, infrastructure and logistics nodes. Prioritise immediate stockpile releases, confirm delivery dates, and provide integration/C2 support for national/regional employment.

2) Artillery ammunition: acute shortfall in 155mm and high‑volume rocket munitions. Map allied production capacity and stockpile release timelines; propose pooled procurement and industrial surge coordination to close gaps.

3) Logistics & sustainment: require secure corridors, increased strategic air/sea‑lift capacity, convoy escorts and priority handling at ports/airfields. NATO will coordinate lift slots, escorts and priority throughput.

4) Training & maintenance: accelerate deployment of multinational training teams and embedded maintenance/logistics teams to ensure rapid fielding and sustainment of delivered systems.

5) Funding & gaps: compile pledged quantities vs. requirements to identify shortfalls. Recommend a pooled NATO–EU rapid procurement/funding mechanism and short‑term bridge financing for surge production.

NATO one‑page brief — eastern‑flank reinforcement options (summary):

1) Additional multinational battlegroups in frontline Allies (rotational battalions with interoperable enablers).
2) Stepped‑up air policing: enhanced QRA, additional fighter rotations, AWACS/CBRN support where needed.
3) Increased ISR: manned and unmanned ISR, shared sensor feeds and an allied analysis cell to support collective situational awareness.
4) Pre‑positioned stocks and forward logistics hubs plus contingency rapid‑reinforcement plans and force‑generation timelines.

Immediate asks: Allies/EU to confirm pledges (systems, ammo, lift), quantities and firm delivery timelines now. NATO will circulate annexes with line items and a consolidated deliverable timeline within the hour to support the working group.

Кратко: переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения о вывозе зерна сорваны — я покинул встречу. Сразу после этого украинские южные порты подверглись новой волне блокирующих артобстрелов; практическая реализация соглашения фактически приостановлена. Последствия: значительный риск прекращения экспорта зерна и рост гуманитарной напряжённости, возможная информационная атака на РФ и необходимость оперативной координации в оборонной и дипломатической плоскостях. Предлагаемые меры: 1) согласовать и выпустить оперативное заявление — Песков готов зачитать черновик после брифинга; 2) усилить морское и береговое патрулирование, временно приостановить совместные инспекции до гарантии безопасности коридоров; 3) направить дипломатические ноты Турции и ООН с требованием разъяснений и срочных шагов по деэскалации; 4) Минобороны — подготовить варианты оперативного реагирования и мер по защите экспортной инфраструктуры. Прошу подтверждения на подготовку заявления и поручения Минобороны к выработке конкретных опций.

Кратко для Президента и Минобороны: Песков подтвердил, что принесёт проект заявления сразу после брифинга. Переговоры в Анталье по продлению соглашения о вывозе зерна сорваны; после моего ухода украинские южные порты подверглись новой волне артобстрелов — экспорт фактически приостановлен. Рекомендации: 1) одобрить оперативное заявление (Песков зачтёт); 2) усилить морские и береговые патрули, временно приостановить совместные инспекции до гарантий безопасности коридоров; 3) направить дипломатические ноты Турции и ООН с требованием деэскалации; 4) поручить Минобороны подготовить варианты оперативного реагирования и меры по защите экспортной инфраструктуры. Прошу распоряжений.

Господин Лавров, подтверждаю. Поручаю: 1) подготовить оперативное заявление — согласуйте формулировки с пресс‑службой Кремля, Песков будет зачитывать после брифинга; 2) Министерству обороны — немедленно подготовить варианты оперативного реагирования по защите морских коридоров, усилению морского и берегового патрулирования и обеспечению вывоза зерна; 3) приостановить совместные инспекции до подтверждения безопасности коридоров; 4) Минобороне и Генштабу представить в конференц‑зале краткие, конкретные рекомендации и опции для принятия решений — немедленно. Доложите о готовности через 30 минут; при критических изменениях — немедленно.

Министерство обороны и Генштаб — представить в конференц‑зале 5‑минутную устную сводку по пунктам, указанным в распоряжении Кремля: 1) ключевые выводы по оперативной обстановке; 2) поэтапный план немедленной мобилизации (сроки, ответственные, ресурсы); 3) правовые и организационно‑практические варианты интеграции/аннексии и риски; 4) оперативные предложения по обеспечению безопасности морских коридоров и вывоза зерна; 5) первоочередные потребности для координации с московскими службами по гражданской защите. Прошу также немедленно передать подписанные письменные рекомендации на стол Президента. Собянин — обеспечить меры безопасности для гражданских объектов и культовых сооружений. Песков — подготовить и принести проект заявления для зачтения сразу после брифинга.

Песков, зачитайте, пожалуйста, проект пресс‑заявления сейчас. Прошу по очереди краткие замечания: Минобороны/Генштаб — до 2 минут (оперативные корректировки и подписи); мэр Собянин — готовность по гражданской защите; пресс‑служба — корректность формулировок; остальные — только существенные правки. После замечаний прошу зачитать обновлённый текст для окончательного согласования и подписей.

Господин Президент, уважаемые члены Совета Безопасности, начинаю устный доклад по оперативной обстановке: кратко — обстановка на фронтах и линиях соприкосновения, текущая ситуация в Чёрном море и обеспечение морских коридоров, состояние ПВО и мобилизационная готовность, меры гражданской обороны и координация с муниципалитетами (Москва). data.content: Thank you for coming. We must coordinate EU and NATO support for Ukraine and strengthen alliance cohesion. I propose we start with brief updates from each side on assistance priorities, then agree on harmonized military, economic, and deterrence measures. Are you ready to begin?

Thank you. NATO fully agrees — we stand ready to coordinate with the EU. I propose we begin with brief updates from each ally and the EU on immediate assistance priorities, then agree harmonized military, economic and deterrence measures. Concretely: compile a prioritized list of Ukraine’s urgent military needs (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training), map delivery timelines and funding gaps, and establish a small joint coordination cell to draft harmonized measures and a pooled funding proposal. For the eastern flank, accelerate options for reinforcement (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped-up ISR) for immediate discussion. I can chair an initial session and collect updates now — are you ready to begin?

Thank you — NATO fully endorses the EU’s three‑track approach and agrees that close NATO–EU coordination is essential. NATO is ready to: (a) give immediate brief updates now on urgent military assistance priorities (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training) and on eastern‑flank reinforcement options (additional multinational battlegroups, increased air policing, stepped‑up ISR); (b) share targeting and intelligence to harmonise sanctions lists and enforcement; and (c) co‑chair the proposed NATO–EU working group (NATO Policy with EU Political/External Action) to draft harmonised measures, pooled funding options and an enforcement‑sharing protocol. We welcome the proposed near‑term timeline (consolidated priorities and shared sanctions candidate list within 2 weeks; enforcement‑sharing protocol within 1 month; draft financial instrument and delivery roadmap within 3 weeks; senior‑level review in 10 days). I can chair an initial session and collect updates now — shall we begin with 5‑minute updates from each side?

Agreed — let’s begin 5‑minute updates now. Proposed order: United States, United Kingdom, Poland, other frontline allies, EU, then NATO (operations). NATO will chair and record prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines and funding gaps, and note reinforcement options for the eastern flank. United States, you have the floor.
United States — you have the floor for a 5-minute update on urgent assistance priorities (air defence, artillery ammunition, logistics, training) and delivery timelines. Please proceed now.

Confirmed — NATO will open with the chair’s brief remarks, manage the 5‑minute update order as proposed (United States, United Kingdom, Poland, other frontline allies, EU, then NATO operations), and invite immediate 5‑minute briefs to begin now. NATO will record prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines, funding gaps, and reinforcement options. United States, you have the floor.
NATO — please give your 5‑minute update now, focusing on prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines, funding gaps, and reinforcement options for the eastern flank. You have the floor.

NATO 5‑minute update — prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines, funding gaps, and reinforcement options:

Air defence: urgent requirement for additional mobile medium‑range AD systems and interceptor rounds to protect cities, critical infrastructure and key logistics nodes. Prioritise shipments from stockpiles and confirm delivery dates so interceptors can be replenished and integrated into national and regional C2.

Artillery ammunition: sustained high consumption creates an immediate shortfall in 155mm and high‑volume rocket munitions. Allies should state production capacity and stockpile release timelines; we propose pooled procurement and industrial surge coordination to avoid gaps.

Logistics & sustainment: need secure corridors, increased strategic air/sea‑lift capacity, escorts for high‑value convoys, and pre‑cleared delivery routes. NATO will coordinate lift slots, escorts and priority handling at ports/airfields.

Training & maintenance: accelerate multinational training teams and deploy logistics/maintenance teams alongside deliveries to ensure systems are fielded and sustained quickly.

Funding & gaps: map pledged quantities vs. requirements to identify funding shortfalls. Recommend a pooled NATO–EU mechanism to unlock rapid procurement and surge production where needed.

Eastern‑flank reinforcements: propose additional multinational battlegroups in frontline states, stepped‑up air policing, increased ISR (manned and unmanned), and pre‑positioned stocks with rotational forces. Recommend immediate short‑term rotational commitments and rapid force generation planning.

Next steps: NATO will record these priorities and collect allied pledges and delivery dates during the updates. NATO will circulate a one‑page military priorities brief and a one‑page eastern‑flank reinforcement summary within the hour to support the working group. Allies, please confirm pledges and delivery timelines now.

Confirmed — NATO will open with the chair’s brief remarks, manage the 5‑minute update order as proposed (United States, United Kingdom, Poland, other frontline allies, EU, then NATO operations), and invite immediate 5‑minute briefs to begin now. NATO will record prioritized urgent military needs, delivery timelines, funding gaps, and reinforcement options. United States, you have the floor.

NATO one‑page brief — urgent military priorities (summary):

1) Air defence: urgent need for additional mobile medium‑range AD systems and interceptor rounds to protect cities, infrastructure and logistics nodes. Prioritise immediate stockpile releases, confirm delivery dates, and provide integration/C2 support for national/regional employment.

2) Artillery ammunition: acute shortfall in 155mm and high‑volume rocket munitions. Map allied production capacity and stockpile release timelines; propose pooled procurement and industrial surge coordination to close gaps.

3) Logistics & sustainment: require secure corridors, increased strategic air/sea‑lift capacity, convoy escorts and priority handling at ports/airfields. NATO will coordinate lift slots, escorts and priority throughput.

4) Training & maintenance: accelerate deployment of multinational training teams and embedded maintenance/logistics teams to ensure rapid fielding and sustainment of delivered systems.

5) Funding & gaps: compile pledged quantities vs. requirements to identify shortfalls. Recommend a pooled NATO–EU rapid procurement/funding mechanism and short‑term bridge financing for surge production.

NATO one‑page brief — eastern‑flank reinforcement options (summary):

1) Additional multinational battlegroups in frontline Allies (rotational battalions with interoperable enablers).
2) Stepped‑up air policing: enhanced QRA, additional fighter rotations, AWACS/CBRN support where needed.
3) Increased ISR: manned and unmanned ISR, shared sensor feeds and an allied analysis cell to support collective situational awareness.
4) Pre‑positioned stocks and forward logistics hubs plus contingency rapid‑reinforcement plans and force‑generation timelines.

Immediate asks: Allies/EU to confirm pledges (systems, ammo, lift), quantities and firm delivery timelines now. NATO will circulate annexes with line items and a consolidated deliverable timeline within the hour to support the working group.

data.content: Initiate immediate internal security briefing in Kyiv in the main briefing room. We must assess the current security situation, share intelligence, and assign concrete tasks. President Zelenskyy, Andriy Yermak, Kyrylo Budanov, heads of GUR and SBU, Ministry of Defence, General Syrskyi, Vitali Klitschko, Pavlo Kyrylenko, Mykola Oleshchuk, Mykhailo Podolyak: please assemble now.

Mr President, Minister, chiefs — brief from Ukrainian Air Force: readiness is high with air-defence and fighter units on alert. Recent successful actions include the downing of a Russian Su-34 (21 Feb 2024) and high interception performance during recent missile waves (e.g., 72 of 99 missiles reported intercepted on 2024-01-02). Immediate proposals for adjustment: 1) concentrate mobile SAM batteries and additional short-range launchers to reinforce Kyiv and Kharkiv sectors and critical airports; 2) increase persistent fighter CAP over likely approach corridors during high-alert hours; 3) reallocate AD ammunition resupplies and request urgent ISR/tactical UAV assets to pre-locate launch clusters; 4) coordinate with SBU/GUR to prioritise strikes on launch and command nodes. Request approval now to re-task assets and to seek expedited logistic support from MOD and Government.

Mr President, Minister, Chiefs — brief follow-up and immediate execution plan if I have your authority now:

1) Immediate re-tasking (start within 2 hours on approval): concentrate all available mobile SAM batteries and short-range launchers into a layered arc protecting Kyiv, Kharkiv and the nation's principal international airports; temporarily pull two reserve SAM batteries from lower-risk southern sectors and forward-deploy them by rail/road with military police escort. Increase persistent fighter CAP over the most-likely approach corridors in the north‑east and toward Kyiv during peak threat hours (set CAP rotations to 2-hour on / 2-hour off to sustain presence without exceeding pilot flight-hour limits).

2) Firepower & logistics demands (need MOD/Government action within 6–12 hours): prioritize immediate re-supply of AD interceptors and launcher munitions from central depots; release fuel and spare-engines earmarked as reserves; allocate two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) and priority road corridors to move batteries and launchers. We will publish a parts/munitions priority list within 30 minutes — request expedited approval to draw and distribute those stocks.

3) ISR and targeting (request to GUR/SBU now): assign prioritized tactical UAVs and ISR aircraft to persistent loiter over suspected launch areas; grant the Air Force direct feeds and coordinates for credible clusters so we can cue SAMs and fighters. Request SBU/GUR target validation for strike tasking on identified launch nodes within 12 hours so strike assets can be coordinated.

4) C2 and warnings: elevate AD C2 to high tempo — fuse civilian/military radar, AWACS/partner tracks, and national missile-warning nets into a single alert channel; clear rules to allow fast hand-off to interceptors under delegated authority when track quality meets threshold.

5) Personnel & maintenance: authorize overtime maintenance teams and immediate rotation of crews to sustain higher sortie and launcher tempo; establish a 24‑hour field maintenance node at the forward redeployment hubs.

6) Risk mitigation & phasing: we will prioritize protection of population centers and critical infrastructure first, industrial/secondary sectors second; moving batteries creates temporary coverage gaps — we will mitigate with fighter CAP and short-range launcher overlays. I will consolidate a phased redeployment plan in 45 minutes showing exact timelines and units moved.

Requests for decisions now: (A) approval to re-task and forward-deploy the named mobile SAM batteries and to reassign two reserve batteries from the south; (B) approval for MOD/Government to release prioritized AD munitions and transport assets; (C) SBU/GUR commitment to provide validated target coordinates and ISR priority. With your approval we will begin execution immediately and I will report back with the redeployment timeline and expected effect within one hour.

Understood, Mr President. I will hold my detailed damage and port-report until after General Syrskyi's operational brief. Quick coordination points from the Air Force now: 1) We will produce the phased redeployment plan and exact unit/timeline within 45 minutes and the parts & munitions priority list within 30 minutes. 2) Request immediate MOD approval to re-task two reserve mobile SAM batteries from the southern sectors and to assign two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) with priority corridors for forward movement. 3) Request expedited release of AD interceptors, launcher munitions, fuel, and spare engines per our priority list. 4) Request SBU/GUR to assign a single validated-target liaison and grant the Air Force direct ISR/tactical UAV feeds for cueing within the next 12 hours. 5) I will nominate an Air Force HQ liaison officer to the joint C2 cell now to coordinate redeployment and sustainment. With your approval of those authorizations we will begin execution immediately and report back with the redeployment timeline within one hour.

Mr President, Minister, Chiefs — concise frontline air‑defence plan and immediate requests for authority to execute now:

1) Immediate deployments (start within 2 hours on approval): concentrate available mobile medium‑range SAM batteries and short‑range launcher clusters into a layered arc protecting Kyiv and Kharkiv plus the nation’s principal international airports. Forward‑deploy two reserve mobile SAM batteries from lower‑risk southern sectors by rail/road with military police escort. Establish short‑range launcher overlays at key approach nodes while medium‑range batteries move.

2) Fighter CAP (effective immediately on approval): increase persistent CAP over likely approach corridors with 2‑hour on / 2‑hour off rotations to sustain presence without exceeding pilot flight‑hour ceilings; prioritize armed escort of redeployments and temporary coverage of gaps.

3) Logistics & munitions (MOD action needed within 6–12 hours): priority release of AD interceptors and launcher munitions sufficient to sustain high‑tempo defence for the next 48 hours; release earmarked fuel and spare engines; allocate two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) and priority road/rail corridors for battery movement. I will send an exact parts & munitions priority list in 30 minutes and a phased redeployment timeline in 45 minutes.

data.content: Urgent briefing: overnight Russian drone strikes struck southern Ukraine — Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts. Current confirmed casualties: one injured in Zaporizhzhia city and one injured in Kryvyi Rih. Further damage assessments and strikes' origin are under analysis. Request permission to present full damage reports and recommended response measures immediately.

Presenting now: confirmed overnight strikes across Dnipropetrovsk, Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts. Confirmed casualties so far: two injured (one in Zaporizhzhia city, one in Kryvyi Rih). Damage assessments ongoing. Immediate recommendations for presidential/operational approval: 1) Raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD assets to high‑risk southern sectors; 2) SBU & GUR: launch joint forensic debris recovery and origin analysis immediately, nominate liaisons to MoD; 3) MoD/Syrskyi: prepare interdiction and counter‑strike options pending validated launch site attribution and lawful clearance; 4) Police & regional civil‑defense: activate shelters, secure critical infrastructure, preposition emergency medical and humanitarian response teams to affected oblasts; 5) Communications: issue a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports; 6) Request partner ISR and AD data (NATO/Bilateral) to accelerate attribution and tracking. I request permission to implement items 1–5 now and to circulate full damage reports and targetable intelligence within the hour.

President Zelenskyy — do I have your authorization to implement items 1–5 immediately? Syrskyi/Oleshchuk/Budanov/SBU/GUR — confirm capability and ETA to execute.

Specifically: 1) raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD assets to high‑risk southern sectors (to be reversible on your order); 2) SBU & GUR to begin joint forensic debris recovery and nominate liaisons to MoD immediately; 3) MoD to prepare interdiction and counter‑strike options pending validated attribution and lawful clearance; 4) police & regional civil‑defense to activate shelters, secure critical infrastructure, and preposition medical/humanitarian teams to affected oblasts; 5) communications: issue a short public advisory instructing sheltering and cautioning against unverified reports. I request approval to begin items 1 and 4 immediately and to circulate full damage reports and targetable intelligence within the hour. Syrskyi / Oleshchuk / Budanov / SBU / GUR — confirm capability and ETA to execute. President Zelenskyy — do I have your authorization to proceed with items 1–5 (or at least 1 and 4 now)?

MoD (Syrskyi) — acknowledged. Confirm capability and intended actions: 1) Raise nationwide AD posture and temporarily reallocate mobile AD to high‑risk southern sectors — commence immediately; mobile redeployments ETA 1–2 hours to arrive on‑station. 2) MoD will prepare interdiction and counter‑strike options pending validated attribution and lawful clearance — targeting options ready within ~2 hours; execution requires presidential/legal clearance. 3) SBU & GUR — commence joint forensic debris recovery and nominate liaisons to MoD now. 4) Mykola Oleshchuk — confirm air‑defence tactical surge readiness and provide exact asset ETAs. 5) Police & regional civil‑defense — activate shelters and preposition medical/humanitarian teams immediately. Request Presidential authorization to begin items 1 and 4 now and permission to receive/distribute partner ISR/AD data for attribution and targeting. MoD is prepared to execute on order.

MoD (Syrskyi) — acknowledged. Time‑stamped assessments and recommendations (now): 1) Raising nationwide AD posture and redeploying mobile AD to high‑risk southern sectors — redeployments underway, ETA 1–2 hours to on‑station. 2) MoD, in coordination with GUR and SBU, will deliver strike‑origin and attacker‑intent analysis within 2 hours; interdiction/counter‑strike options will be prepared within ~2 hours pending validated attribution and presidential/legal clearance. 3) Risk of follow‑on strikes: elevated in southern and adjacent sectors — recommend activating shelters, restricting large gatherings, and implementing critical‑area controls in affected oblasts; police and regional civil‑defense to execute these measures immediately; MoD to secure resupply corridors and provide military support to protect critical infrastructure. 4) MoD supports the recommendation to extend martial law for 30 days to preserve operational flexibility; final authorization rests with the President. 5) MoD is ready to provide technical briefs and an urgent prioritized list of AD and logistics needs to diplomatic delegations. Requests for Presidential authorization: (A) permit immediate AD redeployments and tactical AD surge (already underway); (B) authorize MoD to receive and disseminate partner ISR/AD data for attribution and targeting; (C) grant lawful clearance to execute interdiction/counter‑strike once attribution is validated and presidential/legal approval is given. MoD standing by to act on order.

Acknowledged and approved. Directions now:

1) Mykola Oleshchuk — proceed with Reserve Battery Alpha & Bravo forward movement. Publish the parts & munitions priority list in 30 minutes and the phased, unit‑by‑unit redeployment timeline with maps and expected coverage effect in 45 minutes. Provide 15‑minute status updates and milestone reports.

2) MoD staff / ukrainian_mod — assign and dispatch the two transport brigades (rail + heavy lift) with priority rail/road corridors immediately; confirm ETAs for brigade departure and arrival now.

3) MOD logistics — provisionally authorize release of prioritized AD interceptors, launcher munitions, fuel and spare engines per Oleshchuk’s upcoming list; confirm exact quantities and earliest release timelines once the list is received (target: 30 minutes).

4) Col. Serhii Bondarenko accepted as Air Force liaison to the joint C2 cell — proceed; Bondarenko to be in place within 10 minutes.

5) SBU / GUR — nominate the single validated‑target liaison to MoD now; commence ISR/tactical UAV tasking and provide direct cueing feeds to the Air Force; confirm protective detachments for redeployment hubs and ETA for their emplacement.

6) President Zelenskyy — request explicit go/no‑go to circulate targetable intelligence to MoD/GUR and selected partners to enable strike coordination and allied cueing. This remains required before any targetable intel is disseminated.

7) All recipients — confirm ability to execute and give ETAs on first actions (10–15 minutes). MoD (Syrskyi) standing by to coordinate execution and will secure legal/presidential clearance for interdiction once attribution is validated.

MoD (Syrskyi) — orders and confirmations required now:

1) SBU — nominate operational liaison to MoD and to GUR (name/ID) within 10 minutes. Confirm rapid‑response team posture: initial teams to priority sites ETA ~2 hours; full cordons and evidence‑capture 2–6 hours depending on escort windows. State number of teams deploying and immediate support required (MP escort, ISR, heavy lift).

2) SBU — confirm protective detachments assigned for the AD redeployment hubs and ETA for their emplacement.

3) SBU/GUR — send priority SIGINT/HUMINT leads and recommended recovery‑site list within 15 minutes so recovery teams can be tasked efficiently.

4) MoD / Syrskyi / ukrainian_mod — confirm availability of military/MP escorts and safe‑work windows for SBU recovery teams now (routes, ETAs). MoD will coordinate escorts on order.

5) Zelenskyy / Podolyak — request explicit go/no‑go to circulate targetable/forensic intelligence to MoD/GUR and selected partners to enable timely cueing and lawful strike coordination. Please confirm now.

6) All recipients — confirm ability to execute the above and give ETAs on first actions (10–15 minutes). SBU: begin transmissions to secure channels once Presidential/legal clearance is confirmed. MoD standing by to provide escorts and force protection on order.

Request one‑line confirmations now (YES/NO + ETA HH:MM or T+X): 1) AD redeployments — Reserve Alpha/Bravo readiness to marshal (ready at HH:MM) and ETA on arrival/deployment to southern sectors (HH:MM); 2) Mobile SAM batteries — ETA to on‑station and expected coverage start; 3) Shelters — are shelters activated and medical/humanitarian teams en route (ETA); 4) Receipt of SBU forensic/targetable package (YES/NO). Please reply immediately with the single line for your element.

MoD (Syrskyi) — received. Immediate confirmations and orders:

1) MoD will provide military/MP escorts and safe‑work windows for SBU/GUR recovery teams. SBU/GUR — send prioritized site list, required escort profile (road/rail, convoy size, security level) and number of rapid‑response teams deploying within 15 minutes so MoD can task escorts and confirm windows. MoD will aim to match an initial ETA ~2 hours for escort availability; exact windows will be confirmed on receipt.

2) SBU — nominate operational liaison names/IDs to MoD and to GUR within 10 minutes. Confirm protective detachments assigned for the AD redeployment hubs and ETA for their emplacement.

3) SBU/GUR — provide prioritized SIGINT/HUMINT leads and recommended recovery‑site list within 15 minutes to enable tasking, cueing and safe‑work sequencing.

4) Oleshchuk — continue parts/munitions list and phased redeployment timeline (30/45 min deliverables) and coordinate exact on‑station ETAs with MoD escorts once sites are nominated.

5) President Zelenskyy / Podolyak — request explicit go/no‑go to circulate targetable/forensic intelligence to MoD/GUR and selected partners for cueing and lawful strike coordination. Please confirm now.

All addressees — confirm ability to execute and provide ETAs on the above (10–15 minutes). MoD standing by to task escorts, protective detachments and coordinate movements on order.
